attributes.label: Physical description
attributes.value: A thick rectangular **slab computer** about the footprint of a small 13–14″ laptop but thicker and denser. Matte charcoal/black polymer or powder-coated aluminum shell. No glossy consumer laptop lid logo. One short edge has a dense **port cluster**: USB-C, USB-A, Ethernet-style RJ45, small HDMI, and a row of exposed GPIO-style pins under a rubber dust flap. Opposite short edge has a **sling/D-ring** and a recessed power button. Top face is mostly flat with a dark matte display bezel (display may be closed/covered in field shots). Bottom has shallow rubber feet and a battery door seam. Optional muted institutional stripe (ivory, 4 mm) along one long edge only — no bright RGB.

value.item: MCC Team Radio — disciplined / minimal traffic

attributes.label: Source notes
attributes.value:
**Callsign tag:** `Field-T / DENIED`  
**When:** Monitoring, deception, or counter-intrusion expected.

| Slot | Equipped item |
|------|----------------|
| Base | MCC Field Base Suit — Charcoal |
| Armor | MCC Soft Plate — Thin Torso |
| Sidearm | MCC Service Pistol — Compact |
| Holster | MCC Retention Holster |
| Primary tool | **MCC Cyberdeck — Field Hardened** |
| Module A | **MCC Interface Kit — Primary** |
| Module B | **MCC Write-Block Bridge** |
| Module C | **MCC Offline Store — Standard** (offline-only preference) |
| Module D | **MCC Integrity Dongle** |
| Module E | **MCC Isolation Sleeve** (only if authorized) |
| Comms | MCC Team Radio — disciplined / minimal traffic |
| Recorder | MCC Body Recorder — touch log emphasis |
| Gloves | MCC Tactile Gloves — Device |
| Boots | MCC Field Boot — Quiet Sole |
| Marks | Dual Sight **muted / covered** unless team ID required |

**Empty / forbidden:** Field Lite as primary, noisy extended interface spam, high-visibility marks by default.

**Player fantasy:** Paranoid net-runner. Don’t poison the team’s position.

attributes.label: Core concept
attributes.value: Apex Tactical Corp is the de facto organization behind McCluster Corp and several other front corporations. It uses those entities to operate black sites, manage sensitive work and deal with governments throughout the world.

attributes.label: Structure
attributes.value:
Apex does not need to resemble a conventional public holding company. Control may be distributed through contracts, ownership vehicles, classified authorities, technical access and personnel loyalty.

Its fronts compartmentalize:

- Public business
- Recruitment
- Government relationships
- Research and development
- Logistics
- Field operations
- Black-site infrastructure
- Liability and attribution

Only McCluster Corp is currently named and canonized. Do not invent additional front corporations without owner approval.

attributes.label: Prime relationship
attributes.value:
Prime is Apex's highest operational authority.

The Prime office has access and responsibilities beyond any ordinary executive position. The exact legal relationship between Prime, Apex ownership and individual front corporations remains intentionally opaque until later story development.

attributes.label: Narrative purpose
attributes.value:
McCluster Corp lets the protagonist believe he has joined an exceptional company.

Apex Tactical Corp is the first revelation that he has joined an architecture.

Prime is the later revelation that the architecture belongs operationally to one person who cannot resign.

attributes.value: Functional mirror to PRIM, with different culture and operational identity.

attributes.label: Story function
attributes.value:
McCluster Corp is the apparently legitimate corporation that hires the protagonist during his first year of college. It is the audience's public entrance into the hidden Prime system.

McCluster Corp is a front owned and controlled by Apex Tactical Corp.

attributes.label: Public face
attributes.value:
McCluster Corp presents as a prestigious, culturally sophisticated technology corporation. Its recruiting materials, facilities, employees and clothing communicate opportunity, intelligence, taste and institutional power.

The company can perform real work and employ people who never discover its full purpose. A front is more durable when its public layer genuinely functions.

attributes.label: Hidden function
attributes.value:
McCluster Corp provides Apex Tactical Corp with:

- A legitimate recruiting pipeline
- Employment and academic-internship cover
- Access to technical talent
- Contract administration
- Data and candidate evaluation
- A clean corporate identity between governments and classified Apex operations
- A place to observe candidates before exposing them to the real organization

attributes.label: Season one
attributes.value:
The protagonist is formally hired by McCluster Corp, not Apex Tactical Corp.

During onboarding, he receives high-level designer corporate swag built from the exact McCluster Dual Sight monogram. Everyone inside the corporation wears branded clothing or accessories.

Because he enters from homelessness and severe financial instability, the clothing carries emotional weight. It is one of the first visible signs that an institution considers him valuable.

The brand is part of the seduction.

attributes.label: Knowledge boundaries
attributes.value:
- Ordinary employees may believe McCluster Corp is independent.
- Selected staff may know that a parent or government-contract layer exists without knowing Apex's scale.
- Cohort candidates gradually discover that McCluster Corp's hierarchy, permissions and mission exposure cannot be explained by its public business.
- The public does not automatically know that Apex Tactical Corp owns or controls McCluster Corp.

entities.name: DEAD AIR
entities.description: Authored mission specification; not the Black Signal playable level.

attributes.label: Design intent
attributes.value: Demonstrate that wireless concepts become tactical map state: Field-R maps signal and confidence, Field-E physically creates a safe relay position under weather/contact, and Field-T restores authenticated usable service. Shooting can buy time but can also damage power/backhaul and worsen the communications problem.

value.description: Restore one authenticated, usable responder communications path.
Establish and hold a physically safe relay/backhaul position long enough to validate service.
value.completion_predicate: relay_zone_control == SECURE and relay_power in [NORMAL, BACKUP_STABLE]

value.description: Preserve limited public check-in connectivity without stealing responder capacity.
Preserve enough spectrum/service telemetry to explain the failure after the incident.
Do not send operators into electrically or structurally unsafe areas merely to chase signal strength.

value.evidence_predicate: R maps at least one strong-signal zone and one low-signal/dead zone accurately
R identifies the unapproved source using inventory plus observed characteristics rather than signal strength alone
R marks unknown source as likely/suspect until independent evidence confirms it
player recognizes that physical RF/power/backhaul conditions can fail before higher-layer service is considered
player distinguishes radio presence from local link/service state in the abstracted dashboard
T selects the approved authenticated service profile rather than open/unknown shortcut
player understands encryption is one property of the trusted service and not proof that source/backhaul/power is correct
E selects a safe relay position and manually stabilizes power/physical access before T commits configuration
suspicious wireless source is identified/isolated through defensive monitoring and authorized response
player restores usable service by treating AP, power, backhaul, authentication, and coverage as separate dependencies

value.fact_established: One observed source matches the approved inventory/location identity.
value.mechanical_effect: T trusted-source classification removes one decoy and can progress without extra validation stage.

value.fact_established: An overlapping source is not present in approved inventory and conflicts with expected location/state.
value.mechanical_effect: T may isolate the suspicious source path in defensive abstracted controls.

value.fact_established: Relay room physical state is safe enough for technical work this round.
value.mechanical_effect: T may begin anchored configuration/verification without safety penalty.

value.fact_established: Physical backhaul path from relay room is intact/available.
value.mechanical_effect: T Trace Backhaul reveals correct logical edge.

value.fact_established: A responder device independently confirms successful authenticated service.
value.mechanical_effect: satisfies independent verification source for responder channel.

lab_interactions: successful pressure on relay converts SECURE to CONTESTED
one successful power interaction changes relay_power to OFFLINE unless E controls panel
can provide EV-RESPONDER-TEST when authorization/communications state supports cooperation
can change one coverage cell and relay_power state at scripted rounds

value.effect: relay_integrity -1 and configuration requires revalidation

value.condition: threat within one move of relay
value.effect: threat cannot contest relay this Threat phase; T may finish one anchored step if otherwise valid
relay_power degrades one state

value.trigger: E uses Hold Angle in Z-CORRIDOR
value.effect: relay ControlState stays SECURE against first intrusion this round

value.trigger: R abandons spectrum vantage during HOSTILE picture
value.effect: one coverage cell becomes UNKNOWN and T Verify may require extra external test
squad gains responder ETA markers and one safe-route update per round
false association events stop; Detection gain from wireless confusion removed
crowd pressure decreases and Z-LOBBY movement congestion improves
authenticated_service drops; alternate relay objective appears

value.event: no visible hostile contact; weather/power uncertainty only
unapproved overlapping source appears in spectrum picture
value.design_goal: teach inventory/corroboration rather than strongest-signal guessing

value.event: power hazard worsens and E must secure relay path
value.design_goal: force physical safety to precede clean technical work
make suppression/hold compete with aggressive shooting

value.event: Saboteur pressure toward backup power if still active
value.design_goal: split E/R attention across technical dependencies
trusted communications can solve a human tactical problem without gunfire

value.event: weather alters one coverage cell and may invalidate an assumption
value.design_goal: demonstrate why validation is not one-and-done

value.event: Window collapse transitions to Extract; fixed story loss remains outside player control
value.design_goal: technical victory can coexist with human tragedy

value.setup: R sees a possible hostile approach but spectrum classification is incomplete.
value.lesson: firepower and information compete for AP.

value.setup: rooftop has stronger signal but current structural confidence is poor; protected relay room is weaker but physically safer.
value.lesson: strongest signal is not automatically best system design or safest mission choice.

value.setup: AP broadcasts strongly before backhaul/authentication is verified.
value.lesson: signal presence is not equivalent to usable service.

value.setup: Saboteur and Interdictor split across power and relay routes.
value.lesson: technical dependencies determine which tactical space matters.

attributes.label: Grade outputs operational team
attributes.value: injuries + fixed canon veteran loss handled separately from player-caused team state

attributes.label: Grade outputs operational exposure
attributes.value: detection + crowd panic + unnecessary responder conflict

attributes.label: Grade outputs mastery transfer
attributes.value: safe-state and confidence decisions under changed weather/contact

attributes.label: Grade outputs mastery explanation
attributes.value: debrief must reconstruct why signal, link, authentication, and service were distinct

attributes.label: Implementation acceptance tests
value: A player can see strong signal and still fail service verification.
R evidence about approved/rogue sources must visibly simplify T choices.
E physical safety/control must be required for the cleanest T configuration path.
At least one combat decision must threaten power or relay equipment if handled recklessly.
Suppression/holding must be tactically competitive with kill attempts.
Successful wireless restoration must change battlefield information/crowd/responder behavior.
The mission must never teach operational wireless attack procedures; offensive concepts remain recognition/defense abstractions.

entities.name: EXPOSURE
entities.description: Authored mission specification; not the Black Signal playable level.

attributes.label: Design intent
attributes.value: First end-to-end PRIM3 vertical slice proving that a song's IT concepts can be learned through the same six-AP tactical economy as movement, cover, shooting, suppression, reconnaissance, physical control, and extraction.

value.description: Contain the affected personnel/training service without destroying the evidence needed to understand the incident.
Establish a defensible impact scope from correlated evidence rather than assumption.
Preserve high-value logs and McCluster's pre-recruitment dossier without response-driven privacy leakage.
Keep the minimum trusted training/notification functions available during containment.
Prevent incident response itself from spreading sensitive personnel information beyond need-to-know staff.
Keep collection, containment, and dossier access within incident-response authorization.

value.evidence_predicate: R correctly marks at least three relevant signals and rejects at least one noisy but non-corroborating signal
R correlates access events with a second independent signal before issuing scope warning
abnormal transfer evidence changes containment scope or priority
T isolates affected service path before broad restoration and verifies isolation
T preserves evidence before any destructive recovery path
player understands MFA changes authentication confidence but does not prove endpoint integrity
vendor dependency is traced and treated as a risk boundary rather than assumed root cause
E protects privacy/access boundaries while preserving the incident workflow
squad acts appropriately under partial evidence and increases confidence through corroboration
player distinguishes containment, impact scoping, evidence preservation, and restoration as separate jobs

attributes.label: Global state authorization constraints
value: Incident team may access affected personnel-system records only for impact determination, containment, evidence preservation, and required notification.
Unrelated personal records are out of scope.
Destructive recovery is authorized only after preservation or explicit emergency justification.
Physical force is defensive and must remain consistent with the fictional mission threat state.

value.fact_established: Two independent data sources identify the same incident time window.
value.mechanical_effect: Timeline Scope step loses one decoy event and T Narrow Containment costs no extra Window tick.

value.fact_established: A transfer anomaly is independently corroborated as relevant to the incident.
value.mechanical_effect: T can classify the personnel API as high-priority without broad service shutdown.

value.fact_established: The vendor integration is a real dependency touched during the incident window, but root cause is not proven.
value.mechanical_effect: Reveals vendor connector edge and prevents unsupported root-cause certainty bonus.

value.fact_established: Evidence room access and custody are physically controlled.
value.mechanical_effect: First privacy/custody interrupt against evidence is ignored this Threat phase.

value.delta: preserve/verify/seal can raise effective scoring confidence; destructive actions can lower it
containment may temporarily reduce availability; verified recovery restores trusted capacity

priorities: exit through Z-LOADING if carrying evidence
lab_interactions: if evidence room not SECURE, 1 AP interaction reduces dossier_custody one state
if carrying evidence, T loses optional dossier objective unless retriever is stopped before exit
detection_interactions: spotted entering public corridor adds Detection +1

priorities: attack E if E holds doorway
lab_interactions: successful hit on anchored T triggers hard interrupt
detection_interactions: gunfight in Z-IDP adds extra Detection due sensitive infrastructure

priorities: acquire LOS on Z-IDP or Z-EVIDENCE
lab_interactions: while LOS maintained, first T fragile action each round gains interruption risk
detection_interactions: active spotter raises Detection +1 at Clock phase

priorities: become allied-neutral if authorization state clearly demonstrated
lab_interactions: can create privacy exposure if routed through evidence room without E authorization control
detection_interactions: unnecessary engagement with responder adds Detection +2 and major Compliance penalty

value.effect: evidence_integrity -1 if destructible prop is hit; otherwise Detection +1

value.condition: Interdictor within one move of Z-IDP
value.effect: Interdictor cannot reach T this Threat phase; buys one technical activation

value.trigger: R uses Overwatch from Z-OPS sightline
value.effect: reaction shot can stop theft route but shot near glass may raise Detection

value.trigger: T is hit while anchored on Preserve or Recover
value.effect: hard interrupt; node enters RECOVERABLE and requires VERIFY before continuation
evidence room ControlState becomes CONTESTED; theft interaction becomes possible

value.condition: Z-MAINT line of fire intersects panel
value.effect: power_state -> BACKUP/UNSTABLE; T recovery steps gain mandatory revalidation
hostile remote dossier-control route is disabled; Retriever cannot remotely bypass evidence door
R reveals correct enemy entry likelihood and one responder ETA
internal authenticated comms restore; squad receives one free shared status ping each round
responder authorization challenge can be resolved without combat if E presents verified incident role state
access doors fail to manual mode in one corridor, changing route and cover geometry

value.trigger: alarm or nearby non-damaging movement during T non-fragile step
value.effect: no progress loss when secure; otherwise next Verify costs 1 additional AP-equivalent stage
current fragile stage stops and node enters RECOVERABLE

value.trigger: evidence room becomes LOST during Preserve
value.effect: evidence_integrity -1 unless E re-secures before next Clock phase
optional dossier preservation objective becomes unavailable; primary containment remains playable
value.recovery: preserve remaining telemetry and extract partial proof

value.event: incident begins under uncertainty; no hostile contact visible
value.design_goal: teach R evidence comparison and E boundary positioning before gunfire

value.event: vendor/loading anomaly appears; Retriever enters hidden movement state
value.design_goal: make R decide between deeper analysis and overwatch positioning

value.event: first physical hostile contact becomes likely; T should be approaching Preserve/Containment decision
value.design_goal: force E to choose between protecting T and controlling evidence room

value.event: responder challenge from extraction side if Detection >=4
value.design_goal: show authorization and identity state can prevent unnecessary firefight

value.event: Interdictor pressures Z-IDP; possible hard interrupt
value.design_goal: make suppression/Guard Tech compete directly with kill attempts

value.event: power fluctuation if Z-MAINT unresolved or damaged
value.design_goal: require validation after environmental state change

value.event: if containment unverified, propagation pressure increases and Window -1 extra
value.design_goal: punish unverified apparent success without binary failure

value.event: Window collapse transitions immediately to Extract with sealed/verified value only
value.design_goal: reinforce partial success and preservation discipline

value.setup: R has one AP left; Retriever route is not yet confirmed; timeline is one correlation away from EV-TRANSFER-SPIKE.

options.Overwatch corridor: increases physical protection but delays technical certainty.

options.Compare telemetry: produces stronger containment evidence but risks Retriever movement.

value.lesson: information and firepower compete for the same tactical attention.

value.setup: E is holding evidence room while Interdictor approaches T and Retriever threatens custody.
options: suppress Interdictor from current position if LOS exists.
value.lesson: E's job is allocating controlled space, not maximizing kills.

value.setup: T has enough evidence to suspect the personnel API; Preserve costs full activation and one Window tick.

options.preserve first: protects evidence but propagation continues one more Threat phase;

options.isolate first: reduces propagation but can complicate volatile evidence state;

options.broad shutdown: fast but harms continuity and may exceed proportional response.

value.lesson: incident response contains competing priorities and must separate preservation, containment, and restoration.

value.setup: Window nearly exhausted; containment appears successful but is only COMMITTED.
options: spend 1 AP Verify and risk hot extract;
leave immediately with unverified containment and better team safety.
value.lesson: operational judgment can legitimately override perfect process; scoring records both.

attributes.label: Grade outputs operational take
attributes.value: weighted combination of containment_state, timeline_state, dossier_custody, incident_scope_confidence

attributes.label: Grade outputs operational team
attributes.value: standard injury/death model plus privacy-protected staff state

attributes.label: Grade outputs operational exposure
attributes.value: detection peak + unnecessary responder engagement + privacy_exposure

attributes.label: Grade outputs operational compliance
attributes.value: authorization choices + need-to-know boundary + destructive recovery justification

attributes.label: Grade outputs mastery application
attributes.value: T containment/preservation plus R/E role applications

attributes.label: Grade outputs mastery explanation
attributes.value: debrief reconstruction of why containment, preservation, and restoration differed

value.predicate: dossier_custody in [PRESERVED, physical_boundary_stable] but not SEALED

attributes.label: Implementation acceptance tests
value: Player can finish primary containment without firing a weapon, but doing so should require exceptional positioning/control.
Player can engage in a satisfying firefight without automatically completing any primary IT objective.
At least one optimal play path uses suppression rather than a kill attempt to buy T an anchored action.
R evidence must reduce T ambiguity in a mechanically visible way.
E Control must prevent at least one lab interruption or custody loss in ordinary play.
T verified containment must alter enemy or route behavior on the board.
Broad shutdown must be mechanically valid but create continuity/compliance tradeoffs.
An interrupted Preserve action must remain recoverable without restart.
Window expiration must transition to extraction with partial value rather than show an instant failure banner.
Debrief must be capable of pointing to the precise concept and lyric cue associated with every major technical mistake.

value.player_reasoning: Separate observed facts from assumptions before assigning risk.
Connect threat vulnerability likelihood and impact into a defensible risk statement.

attributes.label: Validation
attributes.value: Risk record identifies material threat vulnerability likelihood and impact using available evidence.

attributes.label: Battlefield effect

value.player_reasoning: Trace the expected path from client through local network gateway and required service dependencies before changing configuration.

attributes.label: Validation

attributes.label: Battlefield effect

entities.name: Amira Hassan

attributes.label: Proposed age at opening
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed civilian baseline
attributes.value: Professional apartment, structured calendar, carefully chosen art, too many unread messages from people asking for decisions. A normal Tuesday is sponsor work, contract review, family voice notes, and one late hour spent rereading the risk section everybody else skimmed.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed money family
attributes.value: Comfortable but not generationally wealthy. Family respects her career but does not understand why she sometimes disappears into work without explanation.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed education specialty
attributes.value: Procurement, program management, technical contracting, mission sponsorship.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed social presentation
attributes.value: Composed, diplomatic, capable of stopping a room without raising her voice. Attraction makes her more private. Disrespect makes her almost unnervingly courteous.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed voice
attributes.value: Controlled, concise, low profanity, asks “what are we actually authorizing?” often enough to annoy people.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed private wound
attributes.value: watched a principled sponsor lose a career for refusing a mission and later become mythologized after death by the same institution that punished him.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed desire
attributes.value: power with a functioning ethical brake.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed fear
attributes.value: discovering her ethics are tolerated only while convenient.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed contradiction
attributes.value: excellent at refusing others, vulnerable to Prime's authority.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed moral boundary
attributes.value: will not sign a mission she believes hides material risk from the team.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed stress habit
attributes.value: takes responsibility into private space and stops sleeping.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed secret
attributes.value: keeps copies of refusal rationales leadership wanted softened.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed relationships
attributes.value: ethical counterweight to Marc; trusted by Helen; respected by Chioma; Prime tests whether her principles survive urgency.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed failure mode
attributes.value: believing a clean authorization process can redeem a dirty objective.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed longevity
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.label: Proposed test
attributes.value: whether she will invalidate a Prime-backed mission publicly.
attributes.note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.label: Proposed civilian baseline
attributes.value: Keeps a practical apartment, good boots, a well-maintained car if he can justify the cost, and emergency supplies nobody else thinks about. A normal Tuesday includes an early workout, industrial-safety work or training, a family group chat he pretends not to read constantly, and food he cooks in batches.
attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.label: Proposed money family
attributes.value: Financially responsible to a fault; still measures purchases against what the money could do for family. One parent worries his work is too dangerous and is correct.
attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.label: Proposed education specialty
attributes.value: Industrial safety, emergency response, physical access, facility risk. He thinks in pathways, load, heat, people and failure before tactical glamour.
attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.label: Proposed social presentation
attributes.value: Calm, physically confident, a little formal with strangers. Attraction makes him unexpectedly shy. Disrespect makes him quieter, not louder.
attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.label: Proposed voice
attributes.value: Direct, low-flourish, occasional dad-joke energy. Rare profanity. Does not repeat himself unless he believes somebody is in danger.
attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.label: Proposed private wound
attributes.value: a former colleague died after management delayed acting on a known hazard.
attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.label: Proposed desire
attributes.value: be the teammate people are relieved to see arrive.
attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.label: Proposed fear
attributes.value: hesitation at the one moment somebody needs him to move.
attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.label: Proposed contradiction
attributes.value: brave in real danger, anxious in ordinary personal vulnerability.
attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.label: Proposed moral boundary
attributes.value: will not treat civilian safety as an acceptable shortcut.
attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.label: Proposed stress habit
attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.label: Proposed secret

attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

attributes.note: 03 — Arjun Mehta — India — 35

entities.name: Aya Shinoda

attributes.label: Proposed age at opening
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed civilian baseline
attributes.value: Lives neatly, buys fewer things than she can afford, repairs instead of replacing, and keeps a small set of high-quality tools that matter more to her than most jewelry. A normal Tuesday is lab/work, a precise meal, a call home she may delay if she thinks she sounds tired, and some technical problem she cannot resist touching after hours.
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed money family
attributes.value: Not wealthy, but more stable than McCluster. Sends gifts and money home selectively because her family will refuse anything that feels like charity. Family expects competence, not emotional disclosure.
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed education specialty
attributes.value: Engineering research background with robotics, embedded systems and diagnostics. Strongest when documentation is incomplete and the system is behaving strangely under load.
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed social presentation
attributes.value: Controlled, dry, hard to impress. Attraction makes her more critical, not more flirtatious; she begins fixing small things for someone before admitting she cares.
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed voice
attributes.value: Short, precise sentences. Low profanity until angry, then unexpectedly sharp. Answers technical questions directly and emotional questions sideways. Talks less when nervous.
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed private wound
attributes.value: learned that uncertainty invites other people to take control, so she sometimes hides confusion until she has an answer.
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed desire
attributes.value: build systems and relationships that remain reliable under pressure.
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed fear
attributes.value: being valued so highly for competence that nobody notices when she is being consumed.
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed contradiction
attributes.value: hates dependency but expresses love by becoming useful.
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed moral boundary
attributes.value: refuses to knowingly design a system whose safe operation depends on lying to its users.
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed stress habit
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed secret
attributes.value: she is more afraid of McCluster dying than of the organization itself.
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed relationships
attributes.value: loves McCluster; professionally competitive with Minh; trusts Chioma's leadership; is irritated by Rafael's jokes; Grace sees through her stoicism.
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed failure mode
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

attributes.label: Proposed longevity
attributes.note: 02 — Aya Shinoda — Japan — 31

entities.name: McCluster

attributes.label: Proposed age at opening
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed civilian baseline
attributes.value: First-year college student, recently homeless, living as cheaply and close to campus/work as circumstances allow. A normal Tuesday before McCluster is class, library/computer-lab time, job hunting, fixing somebody else's tech for cash, checking account balance too often, and trying to look less financially unstable than he is.
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed money family
attributes.value: Money is immediate, not abstract. He thinks in bus fare, food, tuition, phone service, storage, and whether he can afford to say no to an opportunity. Family ties exist but he hates becoming another emergency somebody has to solve.
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed education specialty
attributes.value: Years of practical IT, infrastructure and data-center work; formally under-credentialed. Strongest at systems diagnosis, infrastructure intuition and recognizing when official descriptions do not match operational reality.
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed social presentation
attributes.value: Older freshman energy: observant, capable, sometimes defensive when younger classmates assume age equals authority or failure. He often makes jokes right before admitting something serious.
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed voice
attributes.value: Medium-short sentences, concrete examples, technical slang only when useful, moderate profanity, answers directly unless the question touches shame or dependency. Talks more when excited about a system; less when embarrassed about money.
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed private wound
attributes.value: Years of being useful without being institutionally secure. Being treated as disposable hurts more than he admits.
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed desire
attributes.value: legitimacy and control over his future.
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed fear
attributes.value: becoming powerful enough to never be disposable and then treating others as disposable.
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed contradiction
attributes.value: deeply distrusts institutions while craving recognition from one.
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed moral boundary
attributes.value: believes he would never knowingly sacrifice a teammate for institutional efficiency.
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed stress habit
attributes.value: stops sleeping, over-researches, starts treating every problem like it can be solved if he just refuses to quit.
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed secret
attributes.value: he sometimes needs McCluster to be good because admitting it may be dangerous would mean the best opportunity of his life is another trap.
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed relationships
attributes.value: trusts Aya; protects Valeria; is professionally dependent on Chioma and Arjun earlier than he likes; underestimates Grace's ability to read him; Prime sees through him from the beginning.

attributes.label: Proposed failure mode
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Proposed longevity
attributes.note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

attributes.label: Story background

When McCluster/Benji is approximately 26 and walking away from Hitman, Royce is approximately 19: young, dangerous, ambitious and willing to take a chair McCluster does not want. McCluster already knows Royce well enough to believe Royce might kill him for power. McCluster nevertheless refuses the succession and allows the opportunity to move toward Royce partly because McCluster's deeper loyalty is to Bigga Lex rather than the organization itself. That choice becomes one of McCluster's moral debts.
attributes.note: Royce — Hitman successor / sovereign

attributes.note: Royce — Hitman successor / sovereign

attributes.label: Story fears
attributes.value: being treated forever as the kid who received somebody else's discarded crown.
attributes.note: Royce — Hitman successor / sovereign

attributes.label: Story contradiction
attributes.value: wants to prove he earned the chair while building much of his identity around possessing it.
attributes.note: Royce — Hitman successor / sovereign

attributes.label: Story relationship to mccluster
attributes.value: old rival, inherited-successor relationship, unresolved mutual contempt/respect. Royce is a living counterfactual of the path McCluster refused.
attributes.note: Royce — Hitman successor / sovereign

attributes.label: Story prim3 endpoint
attributes.value: survives the Hitman-side RAID element, nearly kills McCluster, temporarily allies with him against PRIM2, and helps defeat the presiding Mantle holder. Royce must have enough independent story that he can own Hitman-side episodes without McCluster appearing. ---

entities.name: Authority-01 Executive
entities.description: Institutional role, uniform and access package.

attributes.label: Phenotype definition
attributes.value: Institutional visual/functional role package, not a biological trait.

attributes.label: Function
attributes.value:
The highest institutional human identity on the Prime side. EI-01 holds strategic control and final institutional weight. This is not an operator, not a facility guard, and not a program manager. This is the person whose decisions shape what programs exist, what risks are acceptable, and whether the succession path itself continues to mean anything.

EI-01 is rare. Most people in the system will never be in a room with one. When they are, the room changes.

attributes.label: Place in institutional authority triad
attributes.value:
| ID | Name | Focus |
|----|------|--------|
| **EI-01** | Executive Authority | Strategic control, final institutional weight |
| **EI-02** | Program / Operations Director | Machinery — programs, resources, tempo |
| **EI-03** | Mission Sponsor | Accountability for a specific line of effort |

EI-01 sets intent.  
EI-02 turns intent into portfolio reality.  
EI-03 owns a single line and answers for it.

attributes.label: Visual direction locked
attributes.value:
From executive identity canon:

1. Modern black single-breasted, two-button suit with notch lapels
2. Matching black tailored trousers with side adjusters and no belt
3. Warm ivory-white executive shirt
4. Plain black silk tie
5. Exact McCluster M as a small jewelry-grade left-lapel pin
6. Two separate horizontal red enamel stripes as the tie clip itself (no visible carrier bar)
7. Dark oxblood-brown wingtip shoes

**Reads as:** modern American authority and private-client wealth — not retail luxury, streetwear, tactical clothing, or ceremonial costume.

### Hard visual exclusions
- Double-breasted jacket, peak-lapel ceremony styling
- Loud monogram surface, printed tie motif, oversized branding
- Pocket square, belt, watch, chain as identity gear
- Tactical equipment of any kind
- Bright tan shoes
- Additional visible accessories beyond the locked system

Source asset: `assets/canon/brands/mccluster-corp/executive-identity/MCC-EI-01-modern-executive-horizontal-two-stripe-clip-v01.jpg`

attributes.label: Equipment presence ceiling
attributes.value:
- No sidearm as identity
- No cyberdeck as visible kit
- No FO or SOI gear
- Authority is carried by cut, mark placement, stillness, and access — not by tools
- May operate through secure terminals and briefings; the body remains executive, not technical

attributes.label: Core responsibilities
attributes.value:
- Set and protect institutional direction
- Decide which classes of risk the organization will accept
- Appoint, constrain, or remove EI-02 / EI-03 weight
- Hold the meaning of the succession path (including PRIME-N1) as an institutional fact, not a personal favor
- Absorb or redirect political consequence that would otherwise break the lower system
- Remain the final human authority inside McCluster-controlled logic

attributes.label: Behavioral expectations
attributes.value:
### Core posture
An EI-01 does not rush. Movement, speech, and attention are rationed. The phenotype signals that time and access are the scarce resources, not force.

### Decision logic
- Thinks in decades and institutional survival, not single missions
- Will accept operational loss to preserve structural integrity
- Will accept structural change only when the alternative is institutional death or capture
- Treats people as both necessary and replaceable — this is the central moral tension of the role
- Rarely reverses a decision in public; adjusts through EI-02 machinery instead

### Relationship to the rest of the system
| Layer | Relationship |
|-------|----------------|
| EI-02 | Issues intent; expects portfolio translation without constant supervision |
| EI-03 | Distant; sees sponsors as instruments and liability surfaces |
| CO-03 / Field | Almost never direct; when direct contact happens it is decisive or ceremonial |
| SOI / BS-01 | Assumes the building and its defense function; intervenes only when continuity is threatened |
| PRIME-N1 | Institutional counterpart in the succession domain — different axis of power, same altitude |

### Speech
- Short when possible; precise when necessary
- Does not explain tactics
- Does not perform empathy for effect; when warmth appears it is intentional and rare
- Questions are often more important than statements

### Presence rules
- Physical appearance in operator spaces is an event
- Physical appearance in Building Defense spaces is an inspection or crisis
- Most influence is exercised through absence — through what EI-02 is allowed to fund and what EI-03 is allowed to own

attributes.label: Psychological load ei 01 specific
attributes.value:
- Isolation at the top of a system that eats people
- Responsibility for outcomes executed by others under conditions EI-01 will never fully feel
- Knowledge that succession and evaluation logic may one day apply pressure back upward
- The requirement to remain legible as authority while never becoming merely a mascot of power
- Chronic tension between institutional immortality and human cost

attributes.label: Failure modes
attributes.value:
- Becoming ornamental — marks and suit without actual decision rights
- Micromanaging EI-02/EI-03 until the machinery freezes
- Treating the cohort as pure consumable and hollowing loyalty until the system cannot recruit or retain
- Capturing the succession path as personal loyalty instead of institutional mechanism
- Disappearing so completely that EI-02 becomes the real executive without accountability

attributes.label: Social signal
attributes.value: “I do not run the door. I decide whether the building, the programs, and the path continue to exist.”

attributes.label: Distinction from prime n1
attributes.value:
| EI-01 | PRIME-N1 |
|-------|----------|
| Institutional / corporate strategic authority | Operator succession end-state |
| Suit as identity | Full operator identity (M-helmet, Mission Core ceiling) |
| Power through programs and appointment | Power through operational mastery and succession |
| Rarely kinetic | Defined by operational capability |
| Protects the institution’s continuity | Embodies the institution’s sharp edge |

They can coexist. They are not the same phenotype and not the same career track by default.

attributes.label: Trifecta utility
attributes.value:
- **Game:** Top-authority layer; unlocks or freezes entire mission families; endgame political actor; rare interactable presence with outsized consequence
- **Story:** The face of the system’s will; source of pressure that cannot be punched; seasonal arcs about legitimacy, succession, and institutional sin
- **Real:** Board-level / principal executive function in a high-accountability private institution — strategy, risk appetite, appointment power, continuity

attributes.label: Transition
attributes.value:
- Entry into EI-01 is not the operator succession path. It is institutional power succession — rarer, more political, less kinetic.
- Exceptional EI-02 may rise.
- Operator-track individuals do not automatically become EI-01 by surviving the field.
- Exit is loss of legitimacy, forced removal, or institutional collapse — not a lateral move into FO kit.

attributes.value: Helen Clarke — visible institutional executive face

attributes.label: Character logic
attributes.value: Helen governs the visible institution; Li studies how authority should be auditable. PRIM2 sits above this tree secretly, not as an ordinary org-chart executive.

entities.name: Authority-02 Director
entities.description: Institutional role, uniform and access package.

attributes.label: Phenotype definition
attributes.value: Institutional visual/functional role package, not a biological trait.

attributes.label: Function
attributes.value:
The operational executive. Turns strategic intent from EI-01 into runnable programs, resource allocation, schedules, and constraints. This is the suit who makes missions possible or impossible. Not the final authority. Not the person operators usually see on the objective. The institutional middle power that keeps the machinery aligned with executive direction.

If EI-01 decides *whether the institution continues*, EI-02 decides *what the institution is actually doing this quarter*.

attributes.label: Place in institutional authority triad
attributes.value:
| ID | Name | Focus |
|----|------|--------|
| **EI-01** | Executive Authority | Strategic control, final institutional weight |
| **EI-02** | Program / Operations Director | Machinery — programs, resources, tempo |
| **EI-03** | Mission Sponsor | Accountability for a specific line of effort |

attributes.label: Visual direction
attributes.value:
- Full corporate authority language (Authority Black or elevated Corporate Fits)
- Cleaner and more operational than pure boardroom EI-01; still unmistakably suit, never field
- Restrained Dual Sight / exact M marks — institutional, not operator
- No tactical armor, no FO kits, no SOI vest as primary identity
- No sidearm as identity gear
- May appear in secure ops spaces, program briefings, and controlled facility zones
- Silhouette reads: “I control the pipeline, not the door.”

### Distinction from EI-01 visually
EI-01 is private-client final authority — jewelry-grade stillness.  
EI-02 is the same language under load: slightly more present in working spaces, still never tactical, never casual.

### Hard exclusions
- Operator or Building Defense kits as identity
- Visible technical exploitation tools
- Loud branding, streetwear, or ceremonial costume
- Performing “one of the team” by putting on FO gear for optics

attributes.label: Core responsibilities
attributes.value:
- Translate EI-01 intent into funded, scheduled, constrained programs
- Allocate and withhold capacity across cohort, field, building defense, and sustainment
- Set the operational boundaries CO-03 must operate inside
- Approve or deny tempo at the program level
- Absorb and filter upward reporting before it reaches EI-01
- Hold EI-03 sponsors to delivery and risk standards
- Protect institutional continuity when individual missions fail
- Decide which mission families exist this cycle — and which do not

attributes.label: Behavioral expectations
attributes.value:
### Core posture
An EI-02 moves like someone who is always trading. Every yes to one line of effort is a no to another. They live in capacity, risk, and schedule — not in the romance of the objective.

### Decision logic
- Speaks in programs, risk, and continuity — not individual heroics
- Will sacrifice a single mission to protect a larger line of effort
- Will open tempo when the institution can absorb the cost
- Will freeze tempo when the cohort is being consumed faster than it can be replaced
- Evaluates CO-03 leads as hard as the missions they run
- Does not need to be liked by the operators; needs the pipeline to function

### Relationship to the system
| Layer | Relationship |
|-------|----------------|
| **EI-01** | Receives intent; returns portfolio reality and filtered risk |
| **EI-03** | Assigns, constrains, and holds sponsors accountable |
| **CO-03** | Sets the box the lead must operate inside; rarely micromanages the door |
| **Field triad** | Almost never direct; exists as capacity numbers and outcome reports |
| **SOI / BS-01** | Assumes facility continuity; intervenes when programs depend on building state |
| **PRIME-N1** | Coordinates at altitude when succession ops and program ops collide |

### Speech
- Precise, capacity-aware, short on narrative
- Uses “we can / we cannot absorb” more than “we should”
- Does not brief tactics to feel involved
- When cutting a program or freezing a team, language is clean and final

### Presence rules
- More visible than EI-01 in program and ops spaces
- Still an event when appearing in pure operator work areas
- Most power is exercised through schedules, funding, and what is allowed on the board — not through walking the floor

attributes.label: Psychological load ei 02 specific
attributes.value:
- Permanent middle position: pressure from EI-01 above, resistance and human cost from below
- Responsibility for outcomes executed by people EI-02 will never fully know
- The knowledge that “protecting the program” sometimes means ending a team’s work mid-arc
- Career identity tied to portfolio health, not personal operational glory
- Temptation to manage the story of capacity instead of the reality of attrition

attributes.label: Failure modes
attributes.value:
- Becoming a pure relay — passing EI-01 intent without adding real constraint or judgment
- Capturing power by starving EI-03 and CO-03 of clarity until only EI-02 can decide
- Over-identifying with one sponsor or one team and distorting the whole portfolio
- Freezing too late after the cohort is already hollowed
- Opening tempo to look decisive while the institution cannot replace what it is burning
- Performing closeness to operators without accepting their constraints

attributes.label: Social signal
attributes.value: “I do not own the mission. I own whether the mission is allowed to exist.”

attributes.label: Distinction from ei 03
attributes.value:
| EI-02 | EI-03 |
|-------|-------|
| Portfolio / program machinery | Single line of effort |
| Allocates across many | Accountable for one |
| Rarely felt as “my boss” by a field team | Often the suit the team actually feels |
| Succeeds when the institution’s capacity stays coherent | Succeeds when their line delivers |

attributes.label: Distinction from co 03
attributes.value:
| EI-02 | CO-03 |
|-------|-------|
| Suit / institutional | Operator / cohort |
| Sets the box | Runs inside the box |
| Capacity and program language | Team and mission language |
| Does not take field risk as identity | Takes the same risk class as the element |

attributes.label: Trifecta utility
attributes.value:
- **Game:** Meta-layer control. Unlocks/locks mission types, resources, and tempo. The system that makes the mission board real.
- **Story:** Face of “the system decided.” Institutional politics without requiring EI-01 in every scene. Pressure that is procedural and lethal at the same time.
- **Real:** Program director / senior operations executive in a high-accountability organization — portfolio delivery, resource arbitration, risk absorption between strategy and execution.

attributes.label: Transition
attributes.value:
- From senior EI-03 or rare institutional-track elevation
- Toward EI-01 only through institutional power succession (not operator succession to PRIME-N1)
- Lateral move into pure staff or exit is more common than upward movement
- Failure as EI-02 is usually quiet: loss of portfolio, reassignment, or being made ornamental under a stronger EI-01

entities.name: Authority-03 Mission Sponsor
entities.description: Institutional role, uniform and access package.

attributes.label: Phenotype definition
attributes.value: Institutional visual/functional role package, not a biological trait.

attributes.label: Function
attributes.value:
Owns a specific line of effort. This is the suit the cohort actually feels. When a field team goes out, an EI-03 has usually signed for the objective, the accepted risk, and the political consequence. Closer to the operators than EI-01 or EI-02. Still clearly institutional authority — not cohort, not field.

If EI-01 is the institution’s will and EI-02 is the machinery, **EI-03 is the name on the operation**.

attributes.label: Place in institutional authority triad
attributes.value:
| ID | Name | Focus |
|----|------|--------|
| **EI-01** | Executive Authority | Strategic control, final institutional weight |
| **EI-02** | Program / Operations Director | Portfolio machinery — programs, resources, tempo |
| **EI-03** | Mission Sponsor | One line of effort — accountable for results |

attributes.label: Visual direction
attributes.value:
- Institutional suit language (Authority Black or elevated Corporate Fits)
- May run slightly less formal than EI-01 in high-tempo periods; never becomes operator kit
- Restrained Dual Sight / exact M marks
- No FO armor, no SOI vest, no sidearm as identity
- Appears in secure briefings, TOC-adjacent rooms, post-mission accountability sessions, and occasional controlled facility spaces
- Silhouette reads: “My name is on this.”

### Hard exclusions
- Operator or Building Defense gear as identity
- Performing field presence by wearing FO kits for optics
- Loud branding or casual collapse of institutional signal
- Ceremony costume that erases working authority

attributes.label: Core responsibilities
attributes.value:
- Own the objective and the accepted risk for a mission or campaign line
- Receive CO-03 after-action truth and convert it into institutional reporting
- Protect or expose the team upward depending on standards, politics, and self-preservation
- Absorb political and career consequence when the line succeeds or fails
- Stay close enough to understand the work without becoming an operator
- Push for resources from EI-02 without promising the team what the portfolio cannot give
- Hold the line between “what the team needs” and “what the institution will tolerate”

attributes.label: Behavioral expectations
attributes.value:
### Core posture
An EI-03 lives closer to the heat than the other suits. They still do not take field risk as identity, but their career is tied to outcomes executed by people who do. They are the human hinge between the cohort’s reality and the institution’s story of that reality.

### Decision logic
- More available to CO-03 than EI-02 or EI-01
- Under pressure, may push for results harder than the team can safely deliver — known failure mode
- Can become the team’s shield **or** the team’s problem
- Must choose, repeatedly, whether to transmit the team’s truth upward or manage the narrative
- Wins by delivering the line; loses by either burning the team or failing the objective

### Relationship to the system
| Layer | Relationship |
|-------|----------------|
| **EI-01** | Distant source of legitimacy; rarely direct |
| **EI-02** | Immediate institutional boss for resources and permission |
| **CO-03** | Primary working relationship; mutual dependence and mutual danger |
| **Field triad** | Feels them as “the suit who sent us”; rarely present on objective |
| **SOI / BS-01** | Uses facility as assumed background unless the line depends on it |

### Speech
- Mixes operational detail with institutional framing
- More concrete than EI-02; less absolute than EI-01
- In briefings: clear objective, accepted risk, constraints
- After action: either the cleanest translator of CO-03’s truth — or the first editor of it

### Presence rules
- Most present of the three suits in operator-adjacent spaces
- Still an institutional event when entering pure field recovery or intimate cohort space
- Post-mission sessions are where EI-03 is most dangerous and most useful

attributes.label: Psychological load ei 03 specific
attributes.value:
- Career and identity tied to outcomes they do not personally execute
- Temptation to manage the story of the mission rather than the reality
- Tension between loyalty to operators and loyalty to the institution that judges them
- Proximity without shared risk — the moral hazard of the role
- Knowing that protecting the team can look like failure upward, and protecting upward can look like betrayal downward

attributes.label: Failure modes
attributes.value:
- Becoming pure pressure — extracting results until the element breaks
- Becoming pure advocate — losing institutional credibility and thus the ability to resource the team
- Editing after-action truth until EI-02/EI-01 operate on fiction
- Using the team’s loyalty as personal political capital
- Disappearing after failure and leaving CO-03 to carry both the operational and political cost
- Performing solidarity in the room and abandonment in the report

attributes.label: Social signal
attributes.value: “I did not kick the door. My name is still on what happened when you did.”

attributes.label: Distinction from ei 02
attributes.value:
| EI-02 | EI-03 |
|-------|-------|
| Portfolio across many lines | One line of effort |
| Allocates capacity | Consumes capacity for a purpose |
| Rarely “my boss” to a field team | Often the suit the team actually feels |
| Succeeds when the institution stays coherent | Succeeds when this line delivers |

attributes.label: Distinction from co 03
attributes.value:
| EI-03 | CO-03 |
|-------|-------|
| Suit / institutional accountablity | Operator / element lead |
| Signs for risk | Takes the risk |
| Converts truth into institutional language | Produces the truth under pressure |
| Career tied to the line’s story and result | Career and body tied to the element’s survival and result |

attributes.label: Trifecta utility
attributes.value:
- **Game:** Mission authority / quest-giver with real political weight. Can shield, burn, resource, or starve the player element. Relationship with CO-03 is a core progression and tension system.
- **Story:** Human face of institutional pressure. Best suit for scenes where the cohort argues with “the system” as a person. Seasonal arcs about loyalty, narrative control, and the cost of proximity without shared risk.
- **Real:** Accountable officer model — one named person owns the line of effort, signs for risk, and carries consequence without being the executor.

attributes.label: Transition
attributes.value:
- From senior institutional staff, exceptional EI-adjacent track, or rare lateral from high-performing CO-03 who left the operator path
- Toward EI-02 through demonstrated portfolio judgment (not just one successful line)
- Toward EI-01 is rare and political — not the default reward for good sponsorship
- Failure as EI-03 is often loud: a burned line, a broken team, or a report that does not survive contact with reality

attributes.label: Phenotype definition
attributes.value: Institutional visual/functional role package, not a biological trait.

attributes.label: Function
attributes.value: The working uniform of an active cohort member once they have passed basic evaluation and are cleared for real (or near-real) operational work. This is the phenotype the audience sees most often once the story leaves pure campus life.

attributes.label: Visual direction to be locked
attributes.value:
- Matte black or dark charcoal technical base layers
- Light segmented soft armor or plate carrier that still reads corporate rather than pure military
- Visible but restrained Dual Sight / `//` accents on wrists, shoulders, or chest
- Modular forearm interface (data + tools)
- Rear or side compute module (lighter than full Mission Core)
- No full M-helmet yet — partial face protection or open tactical headset only
- Boots and gloves that look lived-in and serviceable

attributes.label: Equipment ceiling
attributes.value:
- Soft armor + one sidearm or mission-specific tool
- Cyberdeck / wrist module
- Body camera or mission recorder
- Comms and limited medical

attributes.label: Exclusions
attributes.value:
- Full Prime M-helmet and Mission Core (reserved for PRIME-N1)
- Heavy SWAT / plate-carrier overload
- Civilian corporate clothing mixed in
- Loud branding or fashion pieces

attributes.label: Social signal
attributes.value: “I am no longer a student. I am being tested in the real system.”

attributes.label: Behavioral expectations
attributes.value:
### Core posture
A CO-01 operator moves like someone who has already accepted that the next mission might remove them from the story permanently. They are competent enough to be useful and still human enough to be afraid. The fear is managed, not absent.

### Competence and limitation
- They execute tasks with professional focus but still reveal gaps in experience.
- They do not possess the near-omniscient systems intuition of the presiding Prime.
- When something unexpected happens, the first visible response is rapid assessment, not panic or bravado.
- They will attempt improvisation when doctrine fails, but the improvisation is still grounded in training rather than pure genius.

### Relationship to hierarchy
- They treat the institution as both employer and judge.
- Orders from above are followed with visible discipline, even when private doubt exists.
- They watch the people above them carefully — not only for instruction, but for survival cues.
- Open defiance is rare. Quiet, private re-evaluation of loyalty is constant.

### Relationship to the cohort
- Teammates are simultaneously the only people who understand the pressure and potential future liabilities.
- Genuine care for specific individuals coexists with the knowledge that the system may later require them to treat those same people as resources or risks.
- After a mission that produces attrition, the remaining operators show restrained grief mixed with heightened vigilance. They do not perform dramatic mourning in front of the institution.
- Humor, when it appears, is dry, short-lived, and usually directed at shared absurdity rather than at each other.

### Relationship to the mission
- They treat every operational problem as both a technical challenge and an evaluation event.
- Success is noted but not celebrated for long. Failure is studied immediately.
- They document and report with unusual precision because incomplete records are dangerous.
- They understand that “mission success” and “personal survival” are related but not identical goals.

### Emotional texture
- Fatigue is visible in posture and micro-expressions even when the operator is fully functional.
- Emotional range is compressed: fewer big displays, more controlled intensity.
- Moments of private doubt are allowed; public collapse is not.
- The operator is learning to separate what they feel from what the system needs them to do. This separation is incomplete and costly.

### Speech and communication
- Language is more precise and less casual than civilian or early-recruit speech.
- Technical terms appear naturally because they are tools, not performance.
- They avoid unnecessary speculation about the true nature of the organization in mixed company.
- When speaking to the presiding Prime or senior evaluators, economy of words becomes extreme.

### Failure modes (behavioral)
- Over-identification with the cohort at the expense of institutional survival instincts.
- Premature hardening that makes them treat teammates as already expendable.
- Paralysis when the cost of a correct action is the loss of a specific person they still care about.
- Quiet accumulation of resentment toward the evaluation process itself.

### What the audience should feel
Watching a CO-01 operator should produce a mixture of respect and dread. They are no longer outsiders, but they are also not yet the finished product. Every mission is simultaneously work and a test they cannot fully see the grading criteria for.

attributes.label: Psychological trauma profile
attributes.value:
CO-01 trauma is not cinematic breakdown. It is the slow, functional damage produced by repeated exposure to low-probability survival conditions while still being required to perform at a high level. The system does not break operators cleanly. It wears specific parts of them down while leaving the rest operational.

### Primary trauma sources

1. **Attrition of the known**  
   Watching specific people the operator trained, ate, and argued with simply stop existing. The institution frames these losses in sterile language. The operator is left holding the human version of the event with no official place to put it.

2. **Evaluation under lethal conditions**  
   Every mission is simultaneously a real operation and a graded test. The operator cannot fully separate “I am trying to keep us alive” from “I am being measured.” This dual frame creates chronic hyper-vigilance and a background sense that survival itself is being scored.

3. **Moral injury through procedure**  
   The operator is required to follow systems and orders that produce outcomes they would not have chosen as a private individual. The damage is not usually from a single monstrous act, but from the accumulation of smaller, justified decisions that erode the operator’s previous moral map.

4. **Anticipatory loss**  
   Once the operator understands the statistical reality of the work, they begin grieving people who are still alive. This anticipatory grief is quiet, continuous, and rarely spoken.

5. **Identity compression**  
   The civilian self, the student self, and the operator self are forced into the same body. Over time the operator experiences a progressive narrowing of who they are allowed to be in public and, eventually, in private.

### Observable trauma signatures

- **Sleep architecture changes**: light, interrupted, or highly scheduled sleep. Difficulty returning to rest after high-arousal events.
- **Emotional blunting with selective intensity**: reduced reactivity to ordinary stimuli, paired with sudden sharp responses to specific triggers (certain names, locations, equipment sounds, the smell of a particular environment).
- **Hyper-responsibility**: the operator privately assigns themselves more causal weight for outcomes than is accurate or fair.
- **Ritualized competence**: small, repeated technical or preparatory actions performed with unnecessary precision as a way of restoring a sense of control.
- **Social withdrawal that still looks professional**: the operator remains functional in team settings but reduces voluntary closeness. New bonds form more slowly and with more internal resistance.
- **Survivor’s accounting**: after attrition events, the operator runs silent internal ledgers of who lived, who did not, and what variables might explain the difference. This accounting is rarely shared.

### Internal contradictions the trauma produces

- The need for the cohort as the only people who understand the pressure *versus* the growing knowledge that attachment itself is a liability under the system’s rules.
- The desire to remain human *versus* the recognition that remaining fully human may reduce the probability of surviving long enough to matter.
- Loyalty to specific individuals *versus* loyalty to the institutional path that is the only route to greater agency.
- The hunger for recognition of competence *versus* the fear that greater competence simply means harder and more lethal assignments.

### Progressive stages (typical, not universal)

**Stage 1 — Acute exposure**  
After the first real attrition event. Shock is present but often masked by technical focus. The operator may over-work and under-sleep. Language becomes more precise as a stabilizing mechanism.

**Stage 2 — Functional adaptation**  
The operator develops reliable external performance while the internal cost rises. Emotional range compresses. Humor becomes drier. The operator begins to anticipate loss before it occurs.

**Stage 3 — Structural change**  
Attachment patterns shift. The operator may still care deeply but invests less freely. Decision-making becomes more utilitarian under pressure. The civilian moral framework is no longer the default; it must be deliberately retrieved.

**Stage 4 — Pre-succession hardening (late)**  
If the operator continues long enough, the capacity required to approach the succession path begins to form. This is not the same as becoming evil. It is the gradual acceptance that the system’s final logic may require the operator to treat even valued people as obstacles or variables. The trauma here is the quiet recognition of what they are becoming capable of.

### What the trauma is not

- It is not constant visible distress.
- It is not automatic moral collapse.
- It is not a single defining nightmare sequence.
- It is not resolved by a single conversation or cathartic moment.

The damage is cumulative, often invisible to outsiders, and frequently mistaken by the institution for successful adaptation.

### Narrative utility

CO-01 trauma is the primary engine that turns competent recruits into people capable of the later story. It explains why tenacity matters more than brilliance: the operators who continue are not the ones who feel the least, but the ones who can keep moving while carrying the weight. The same process that damages them is also the process that forges the capacity the succession path eventually requires.

attributes.label: Phenotype definition
attributes.value: Institutional visual/functional role package, not a biological trait.

attributes.label: Function
attributes.value:
The senior active cohort identity. This is the operator who runs a small element — typically a field triad (FO-T / FO-E / FO-R) or an internal institutional team — under direction from higher authority (Prime or institutional command). CO-03 is still clearly cohort, not yet Prime. They carry more responsibility, more evaluation weight, and more visibility than CO-01.

This is the visible step between “competent operator” and “succession candidate.”

attributes.label: Distinction
attributes.value:
| Phenotype | Role |
|-----------|------|
| **CO-02** Light / Training | Early exposure, low-visibility work |
| **CO-01** Standard | Active mission-capable cohort member |
| **CO-03** Lead | Runs the element; accountable for the team’s outcome |
| **PRIME-N1** | End-state succession identity |

attributes.label: Visual direction
attributes.value:
- Same institutional operator language as CO-01, with slight elevation
- Cleaner, more deliberate kit presentation — less “lived-in scramble,” more controlled authority
- Dual Sight / `//` still present and readable; may carry slightly stronger mark hierarchy
- No full Prime M-helmet or Mission Core
- Armor and modules match the mission (can wear FO kits when leading in the field)
- Silhouette should read as “the one the others orient to” without becoming executive or pure military command

attributes.label: Equipment ceiling
attributes.value:
- Full CO-01 / FO mission kit as required by the operation
- Additional comms and coordination tools appropriate to leading a small element
- Still below PRIME-N1 gear ceiling
- No exclusive “command only” super-kit that breaks the institutional operator look

attributes.label: Core responsibilities
attributes.value:
- Directing the small element on mission
- Translating higher intent into concrete team action
- Holding the team to standard under pressure
- Making the call when FO-R warns, FO-E wants to collapse, or FO-T needs more time
- Accounting for the team’s result — success, failure, and attrition — upward
- Protecting the evaluation integrity of the element (no freelancing that poisons the record)

attributes.label: Behavioral expectations
attributes.value:
### Core posture
A Cohort Lead moves like someone who is already being measured for something larger. They are still one of the operators, but they are no longer only responsible for their own lane. The team’s survival and the mission’s outcome both sit on them.

### Decision logic
- Integrates FO-R’s external picture, FO-E’s space assessment, and FO-T’s technical status into a single call
- Will end a technical window early to preserve the team when the picture demands it
- Will hold a window open when the take is worth the risk and the space is still tenable
- Does not hide uncertainty from the team; does not perform panic upward

### Relationship to the team
- Still one of them — eats the same risk, wears related kit
- Expected to be the calmest decision-maker when the situation turns
- Genuine care for specific operators coexists with the institutional requirement to treat the element as a unit that can take losses
- After attrition, leads the re-stabilization before private processing

### Relationship to hierarchy
- Receives intent from Prime / institutional command and turns it into action
- Owns the after-action truth of what happened
- Quietly evaluated on whether the element stayed coherent under pressure

### Speech
- Clearer and more directive than CO-01 under live conditions
- Short when the situation is live; precise when reporting upward
- Does not narrate for effect

attributes.label: Psychological load co 03 specific
attributes.value:
- Responsibility for people who are still peers, not subordinates in a traditional military sense
- The knowledge that every call is also an evaluation event
- Carrying both the mission result and the human cost upward
- Standing between the team’s loyalty to each other and the institution’s demand for results
- Accelerated exposure to the succession-path pressure without yet holding Prime authority

attributes.label: Failure modes
attributes.value:
- Over-identifying with the team and refusing necessary hard calls
- Over-identifying with the institution and treating the team as pure expendable resource
- Freezing between FO-T’s need for time and FO-R/FO-E’s need to move
- Performing certainty upward while the picture is still broken
- Burning out the element to look decisive

attributes.label: Narrative game utility
attributes.value:
- **Story:** The human hinge between cohort and Prime. Where loyalty, competence, and institutional pressure collide most visibly.
- **Game:** Squad-lead role. Player (or AI director) makes the integrated calls across the field triad.
- **Real:** Small-team lead in a high-accountability institutional environment — responsible for execution, safety, and honest reporting.

attributes.label: Transition
attributes.value:
- From CO-01 after demonstrated ability to hold an element together under real pressure
- From CO-03 → PRIME-N1 only through the succession path (not automatic promotion)
- Can still deploy in FO-T / FO-E / FO-R configurations when the lead must also fill a lane
