entities.name: Field Operator (general deployment)
entities.description: Institutional role, uniform and access package.

attributes.label: Phenotype definition
attributes.value: Institutional visual/functional role package, not a biological trait.

attributes.label: Function
attributes.value:
The external deployment phenotype. This is the loadout and behavioral posture used when cohort members (or more experienced operators) are sent outside corporate facilities into real-world operational environments — foreign facilities, contested infrastructure, government-directed actions against adversarial actors, or any mission where the environment is not controlled by McCluster.

This is distinct from:
- **SOI-01 Security Officer** — internal facility and information protection
- **CO-01 Cohort Operator (Standard)** — general mission-capable institutional operator
- **PRIME-N1** — end-state succession identity

FO-01 is what the audience sees when the story leaves the building and enters the field.

attributes.label: Visual direction to be locked
attributes.value:
- Darker, more weathered, and more modular than standard CO-01
- Increased environmental protection (weather, debris, low-visibility)
- Soft-to-mid armor that prioritizes mobility over heavy plating
- Stronger Dual Sight / `//` visibility for rapid team identification in low light or chaos
- Mission-specific modular attachments (breaching, technical entry, surveillance, exfil)
- Face protection short of the full M-helmet (balaclava, partial shell, or advanced headset)
- Boots and gloves rated for real terrain and prolonged wear
- Overall silhouette still reads as high-end institutional rather than generic military special forces

---

attributes.label: Gear specifications
attributes.value:
### Design philosophy
FO-01 gear is **mission-configured institutional equipment**.  
It must remain clearly McCluster in silhouette, materials, and marks while accepting that the field is hostile, dirty, and unpredictable.  
Mobility and modularity outrank heavy protection.  
Every added item must justify its weight and visual noise.

### Equipment Floor (minimum viable FO-01)
Every Field Operator deploys with at least:

| Item | Specification |
|------|---------------|
| Base layer | Dark technical under-suit / combat shirt and trousers, matte finish |
| Armor | Soft-to-mid protective vest or light plate carrier; torso coverage only |
| Sidearm | One compact service sidearm in low-profile retention holster |
| Comms | Secure team radio + bone or in-ear element |
| Recording | Body-worn or helmet/headset-mounted mission recorder |
| Compute | Field cyberdeck or advanced wrist module with offline capability |
| Identification | Visible Dual Sight or red `//` accent for rapid friendly recognition |
| Footwear | Rugged, quiet-soled boots rated for extended wear and mixed terrain |
| Handwear | Tactical gloves compatible with device use and weapon handling |

### Equipment Ceiling (authorized maximum)
The following may be added according to mission profile. Nothing beyond this list is standard.

**Protection**
- Soft armor with optional thin hard plates (front/back only)
- Limited extremity protection (knees, elbows) only when the environment demands it
- Neck or lower-face protection short of a full helmet
- No full ballistic helmet, no riot gear, no bomb suit derivatives

**Head / Face**
- Advanced tactical headset with integrated comms and recording
- Partial protective shell or reinforced balaclava
- Low-profile eye protection / visor
- **Forbidden:** full M-architecture helmet and Mission Core (PRIME-N1 only)

**Core Electronics**
- Field cyberdeck (larger than SOI version, still wearable)
- Redundant encrypted communications
- Mission recording suite (body + optional weapon or tool mount)
- Compact power bank / hot-swap battery system
- Limited electronic countermeasure or signal analysis module (mission-specific)

**Mission Modules** (attach only what the operation requires)
- Technical entry / bypass kit
- Breaching charge or mechanical entry tools (when authorized)
- Surveillance / sensor package
- Forensic imaging or data-extraction tools
- Short-range drone or throwable sensor (rare, high-value missions only)
- Medical blowout kit (individual)
- Signaling and marking devices

**Lethal / Decisive Tools**
- One sidearm (mandatory floor)
- One primary tool or weapon appropriate to the specific task (carbine, suppressed platform, or specialized technical tool)
- No standard issue long gun across the entire phenotype; weapon is mission-selected
- No visible spare magazine farms or excessive external pouches that turn the silhouette into conventional infantry

### Modular Logic
Gear is attached to a clean base chassis (vest + belt + optional light pack).  
Modules are added or removed per mission.  
An operator returning from a technical infiltration should not look identical to one returning from a contested extraction.  
The base identity (silhouette, marks, color language) remains constant; only the modules change.

### Marks & Identity Hardware
- Exact McCluster M appears in restrained, durable form (subdued or tonal preferred in field)
- Dual Sight and/or red `//` must remain readable for team identification in low light
- No non-McCluster patches, flags, or unit insignia
- No morale patches or personalization that breaks institutional uniformity

### Exclusions (hard)
- Full Prime M-helmet + Jetson-class Mission Core
- Clean Corporate Fits (CFI) office garments
- Conventional military plate carriers overloaded with pouches
- Visible ammunition management systems that dominate the silhouette
- Riot shields, batons as primary, or crowd-control equipment
- Any gear that makes the operator read as generic special forces or police SWAT
- Non-canon marks or commercial branding

### Comparison Snapshot

| Element | SOI-01 Security | CO-01 Standard | FO-01 Field |
|---------|------------------|----------------|-------------|
| Domain | Facility | Institutional / mixed | External / uncontrolled |
| Armor | Ultra-thin vest | Light soft armor | Soft-to-mid, modular |
| Primary weapon | Sidearm only | Sidearm + limited tool | Sidearm + mission-selected primary |
| Electronics | Cyberdeck | Wrist module / light compute | Full field cyberdeck + redundant comms |
| Recording | Body camera | Body / mission recorder | Full mission recording suite |
| Modules | Almost none | Minimal | Mission-configured |
| Environmental rating | Indoor / campus | Mixed | Full field |
| Visual noise | Lowest | Low | Controlled but higher |

### Load-bearing principles
1. If the item is not required for the specific mission, it is left behind.
2. Every external pouch or module must earn its place visually and functionally.
3. The operator must still be able to move, climb, enter confined spaces, and operate devices without fighting their own gear.
4. When in doubt, the silhouette should still say “McCluster institutional operator,” not “soldier.”

---

attributes.label: Social signal
attributes.value: “We are no longer inside the system’s walls. The environment is hostile and the evaluation continues.”

attributes.label: Behavioral expectations
attributes.value:
### Core posture
A Field Operator moves with the understanding that the environment itself is an active variable. Unlike facility work, the field does not care about institutional procedure. The operator must remain institutional while the world refuses to cooperate.

### Operational behavior
- Higher baseline arousal than CO-01 inside the building
- Faster decision loops; less time for perfect information
- Strong preference for reversible actions until the point of no return
- Explicit contingency thinking (“if this node fails, we move to…”)
- Reduced tolerance for internal debate once the team is exposed

### Relationship to the environment
- Treats architecture, networks, weather, civilians, and local forces as part of the problem set
- Constant low-level scanning for surveillance, ambush, and technical compromise
- Willingness to abandon gear or change plans when the environment demands it

### Relationship to the team
- Tighter physical and communicative spacing than in facility operations
- Clearer role specialization under pressure
- Faster assumption of leadership if the designated lead is degraded
- After contact or loss, the remaining operators re-stabilize the team before processing emotion

### Psychological load (field-specific)
- Isolation from institutional support structures
- Increased moral complexity when operating among civilians or under foreign legal regimes
- Greater anticipatory stress because extraction is not guaranteed
- The knowledge that failure in the field is harder to conceal or reframe than failure inside a McCluster facility

### Speech and communication
- Shorter transmissions
- Higher use of procedural and brevity codes
- Minimal speculation once the operation is live
- After-action language becomes extremely precise; emotional content is deferred

attributes.label: Distinction from soi 01 security officer
attributes.value:
| Dimension | SOI-01 Security Officer | FO-01 Field Operator |
|-----------|-------------------------|----------------------|
| Domain | Inside / around McCluster facilities | External, uncontrolled environments |
| Primary mission | Protect people, data, continuity | Execute directed external objectives |
| Threat model | Internal breach, access control, cyber | Hostile actors, environment, surveillance, kinetic |
| Gear philosophy | Minimal, professional, cyber-first | Modular, mission-configured, higher risk tolerance |
| Visual signal | Corporate security | Institutional operator in the open world |

attributes.label: Distinction from co 01 standard
attributes.value:
CO-01 is the general institutional operator identity.  
FO-01 is the specialized external deployment configuration of that identity (or of more senior operators).  
A character may wear CO-01 inside the system and FO-01 when sent out.

attributes.label: Transition
attributes.value:
- From CO-01 or CO-02 when assigned to external operations
- From FO-01 back to CO-01 or Corporate Fits when returning to controlled environments
- Long-term or repeated FO-01 exposure accelerates the psychological progression described in the CO-01 trauma profile

attributes.label: Narrative utility
attributes.value: FO-01 is the phenotype that lets the story leave the building. It is what the audience sees during government-directed missions, data-center raids, infrastructure operations, and any sequence where the cohort is operating against a real external adversary. It keeps the McCluster institutional signal while acknowledging that the field is a different, more lethal classroom.

entities.name: Field-E Entry Operator
entities.description: Institutional role, uniform and access package.

attributes.label: Phenotype definition
attributes.value: Institutional visual/functional role package, not a biological trait.

attributes.label: Function
attributes.value:
The physical access and close-security specialist. Responsible for getting the team onto the objective, controlling immediate space, and protecting the Technical operator while the technical work is performed. This is the kinetic and spatial problem-solver of the field triad.

FO-E exists so that FO-T can work. When the technical window is open, FO-E’s primary product is controlled space and time.

attributes.label: Visual direction
attributes.value:
- Highest soft-to-mid armor load of the three basic field phenotypes
- Darker, more aggressive weathering than FO-T; still institutional, never generic special forces
- Strong, readable Dual Sight / red `//` for rapid recognition in confined spaces, smoke, or low light
- Silhouette emphasizes mobility + protection rather than maximum armor bulk
- Gloves and boots built for forced movement, climbing, door work, and close contact
- Face protection short of the full M-helmet (partial shell, reinforced balaclava, or advanced headset)
- Overall look: the person who goes through the door first and holds it

attributes.label: Gear specifications
attributes.value:
### Design philosophy
Gear exists to create access, hold space, and keep FO-T alive and working.  
Every added item must improve entry, control, or protection.  
Bulk that slows movement through doors, stairs, or confined plant rooms is rejected.

### Equipment Floor
| Item | Specification |
|------|---------------|
| Base layer | Dark technical field suit |
| Armor | Soft-to-mid torso protection; highest of the triad |
| Sidearm | One compact service sidearm, low-profile holster |
| Primary | Mission-selected primary tool or weapon (more common than on FO-T) |
| Entry tools | Mechanical entry set at minimum |
| Comms | Secure team radio + reliable earpiece |
| Recording | Body or headset mission recorder |
| Identification | Strong Dual Sight or red `//` visibility |
| Handwear | Impact- and abrasion-resistant gloves that still allow device and weapon use |
| Footwear | Aggressive field boots rated for forced movement and debris |

### Equipment Ceiling (mission-authorized)
**Protection**
- Soft armor with optional thin hard plates (front/back)
- Limited extremity protection (knees, elbows) when the environment demands it
- Partial face / neck protection
- No full ballistic helmet, no riot gear, no bomb-suit derivatives

**Entry & Access**
- Mechanical entry tools (spreaders, breachers, bypass hardware)
- Limited energetic entry tools when authorized
- Door and lock defeat capability appropriate to the target
- Short-range cutting or penetration tools for interior obstacles

**Kinetic**
- Sidearm mandatory
- Mission-selected primary (carbine, suppressed platform, or specialized entry weapon)
- No magazine-farm infantry setups that destroy the institutional silhouette

**Electronics**
- Standard field comms and recording
- Limited personal sensor or short-range detection tools
- No full technical exploitation stack (that belongs to FO-T)

### Hard Exclusions
- Full Prime M-helmet and Mission Core
- Heavy plate carriers overloaded with pouches
- Primary technical exploitation kits (FO-T domain)
- Long-duration observation / sniper-style optics packages (FO-R domain)
- Clean Corporate Fits garments
- Non-McCluster marks or generic special-forces patches

---

attributes.label: Gear loadouts by mission profile
attributes.value:
FO-E does not wear one fixed kit. The base identity stays constant; modules change with the phase of the operation. Below are the four primary loadout configurations.

### 1. Approach & Entry (FO-E-AE)
**Use when:** Moving to the objective and making the initial breach or technical entry.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Soft-to-mid torso; optional thin plates |
| Entry tools | Full mechanical set + limited energetic if authorized |
| Kinetic | Sidearm + mission-selected primary |
| Comms | Full secure team link |
| Recording | Continuous from final approach |
| Identification | Strong Dual Sight / `//` visibility |
| Mobility | Balanced — must carry entry tools without becoming slow in corridors |

**Design note:** This is FO-E at its most tool-heavy. The job is to open the space. Once inside and the door is controlled, excess entry tools can be staged or dropped if they interfere with holding.

---

### 2. Hold & Protect (FO-E-HP)
**Use when:** FO-T is on the target node and FO-E is pure close security — doors, angles, and immediate space.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Soft-to-mid; prioritize coverage over tool bulk |
| Entry tools | Minimal — only what is still needed for interior obstacles |
| Kinetic | Sidearm + primary ready; emphasis on control, not volume of fire |
| Comms | Full link to FO-T and FO-R |
| Recording | Continuous |
| Identification | High visibility for rapid team recognition in confined space |
| Mobility | High within the held space; must be able to shift rooms or collapse fast |

**Design note:** Stripped of pure entry bulk. The product is controlled space and time. Every extra pouch that slows a room-to-room shift is a liability.

---

### 3. Contact / Collapse (FO-E-CC)
**Use when:** The space is compromised, contact has occurred, or FO-R has called an external threat that forces movement.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Maximum authorized soft-to-mid for FO-E |
| Entry tools | Only what is required for the exit path |
| Kinetic | Sidearm + primary; readiness for short, decisive action |
| Comms | High-tempo team link |
| Recording | Continuous through the break-contact |
| Identification | High visibility — team must find each other under stress |
| Mobility | Highest priority — lead the move, keep FO-T moving, break contact |

**Design note:** This is FO-E in emergency mode. Entry tools become secondary. The job is no longer “hold for the technical window”; it is “get the protected asset and the team off the objective alive.”

---

### 4. Technical Escort (FO-E-TE)
**Use when:** Moving FO-T between nodes inside a larger facility, or escorting the technical element during a multi-stage objective where entry is already complete but the space is still hostile.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Soft-to-mid, balanced for movement with FO-T |
| Entry tools | Light interior set (doors, cabinets, secondary barriers) |
| Kinetic | Sidearm + compact primary preferred |
| Comms | Tight link to FO-T; FO-R picture still active |
| Recording | Continuous |
| Identification | Readable Dual Sight |
| Mobility | Matched to FO-T’s pace — never so light that protection is sacrificed, never so heavy that FO-T is delayed |

**Design note:** Hybrid of Hold and movement. FO-E stays glued to the technical element without turning the pair into a slow, over-armored target.

---

### Loadout Selection Logic

| Situation | Preferred Loadout |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Final approach and initial breach | Approach & Entry (FO-E-AE) |
| FO-T working, space still tenable | Hold & Protect (FO-E-HP) |
| Contact, FO-R abort call, or space lost | Contact / Collapse (FO-E-CC) |
| Moving FO-T between interior nodes | Technical Escort (FO-E-TE) |

An operator will typically sequence through these in a single mission: Approach & Entry → Hold & Protect → (optional Technical Escort) → Contact/Collapse or controlled exit.

### Cross-loadout rules
1. Sidearm never comes off.
2. Dual Sight stays readable unless a specific low-signature phase is ordered (rare for FO-E).
3. No loadout may become a full technical exploitation kit or a pure long-range observation package.
4. If the operator cannot move through a standard door or stairwell under control, the loadout is wrong for FO-E.
5. When FO-T is exposed and working, FO-E’s kit must not create noise, snag, or delay that endangers the technical window.

---

attributes.label: Core responsibilities
attributes.value:
- Route selection and physical approach
- Forced or technical entry onto the objective
- Immediate area security once inside
- Close protection of FO-T during the entire technical window
- Control of doors, corridors, stairs, and chokepoints
- Leading movement on contact or emergency exfiltration
- Rapid decision-making about whether the space is still tenable

attributes.label: Behavioral expectations
attributes.value:
### Core posture
An Entry Field Operator treats space as a resource that is constantly being spent. Every second the door is open, every corridor left unsecured, and every angle left uncovered is a cost. The job is to buy FO-T enough controlled space and time to finish the work.

### During entry and on the objective
- Highest baseline physical readiness on the team
- Decisions are spatial and temporal: where to stand, what to block, when to move, when to collapse the perimeter
- Low tolerance for extended technical debate once the team is exposed
- Treats FO-T as a protected asset for the duration of the technical window
- Maintains constant awareness of FO-R’s external picture

### On contact or deterioration
- Prioritizes team integrity and exit over continued objective work unless explicitly ordered otherwise
- Will force movement if the space becomes indefensible
- Does not require perfect information to act; acts on the best available picture and updates in motion

### Speech patterns
- Short, directional, and action-oriented
- Uses clear movement and security language
- Minimal narrative while the situation is live
- After contact, language becomes extremely precise about what happened in the space and what the remaining options are

### Relationship to pressure
- External threat increases tempo rather than producing hesitation
- Visible stress appears as sharper movement and shorter communications
- The operator is expected to remain the calmest body in the room when the room becomes violent

attributes.label: Psychological load fo e specific
attributes.value:
- Responsibility for the physical survival of the technical element
- The knowledge that a single bad angle or delayed movement can erase the entire technical take and the people who produced it
- Repeated exposure to the moment of entry — the highest-risk transition in most operations
- Carrying the immediate human cost when contact occurs (FO-T may still be focused on systems; FO-E is focused on bodies and space)
- Tendency toward hyper-vigilance about doors, corners, and timing that can persist after return to controlled environments

attributes.label: Relationship to the field triad
attributes.value:
| Phenotype | Relationship to FO-E |
|-----------|----------------------|
| FO-T Technical | Protected asset; FO-E’s primary product is the space and time FO-T needs |
| FO-R Recon | Supplies the external warning that lets FO-E decide whether the space is still worth holding |
| FO-E Entry | Creates access, holds the interior, leads movement on contact or exit |

attributes.label: Failure modes
attributes.value:
- Over-focusing on the immediate room and losing the larger exit picture
- Holding a space past the point it is tenable because FO-T is not finished
- Excessive aggression that creates noise or casualties the mission cannot afford
- Under-communicating movement decisions so FO-T and FO-R lose the picture
- Post-mission difficulty standing down from continuous spatial threat assessment

attributes.label: Narrative utility
attributes.value: FO-E is the phenotype for forced entry, corridor tension, and the physical reality that surrounds technical work. It keeps field sequences kinetic and human without collapsing the team into generic special-forces aesthetics. The drama sits in the collision between the need to protect the technical window and the need to keep the team alive when the space turns against them.

attributes.label: Transition
attributes.value:
- From CO-01 or FO-01 when assigned the entry / close-security role on an external mission
- Back to CO-01 or Corporate Fits when returning to controlled environments
- Repeated FO-E exposure accelerates the physical and spatial components of the broader operator trauma profile, with particular emphasis on responsibility for other people’s bodies in confined, hostile space

attributes.label: Function
attributes.value:
The external awareness and early-warning specialist. Responsible for surveillance of the approach, perimeter, and surrounding environment while the rest of the team is on the objective. This phenotype owns the question: “What is about to happen to us from outside?”

FO-R exists so that FO-E and FO-T can stay focused inward. Their primary product is a continuous, accurate external picture and the authority to force a change of plan when that picture collapses.

attributes.label: Visual direction
attributes.value:
- Lightest armor of the three basic field phenotypes for maximum mobility and low visual/thermal signature
- Darker, more subdued weathering; prioritizes blending over presence
- Dual Sight / red `//` is present but controllable — can be muted or covered when signature must stay low
- Silhouette optimized for static or semi-static observation positions and rapid displacement
- Optics and sensor packages are the visual signature more than heavy armor or weapons
- Face protection minimal and low-profile (headset, soft cover, or partial shell only)
- Overall look: the person who is hard to see and harder to surprise

attributes.label: Gear specifications
attributes.value:
### Design philosophy
Gear exists to see farther, stay quieter, and move faster than the threat.  
Observation quality and signature management outrank armor and pure kinetic load.  
Every item must justify itself against the cost of being detected.

### Equipment Floor
| Item | Specification |
|------|---------------|
| Base layer | Dark technical field suit, low-signature materials |
| Armor | Lightest soft torso protection of the triad |
| Sidearm | One compact service sidearm, low-profile holster |
| Optics | Mission-appropriate observation optics |
| Sensors | Basic environmental / approach detection capability |
| Comms | Secure team radio + reliable low-profile earpiece |
| Recording | Observation and mission recording suite |
| Identification | Dual Sight or red `//` that can be subdued |
| Handwear | Low-bulk gloves compatible with optics and device use |
| Footwear | Quiet-soled field boots optimized for movement and static positions |

### Equipment Ceiling (mission-authorized)
**Observation & Sensors**
- Enhanced day/night optics
- Extended-duration observation tools
- Compact sensor packages (motion, acoustic, or simple RF as authorized)
- Recording systems optimized for long takes and evidence-quality capture

**Protection & Mobility**
- Light soft armor only
- Minimal extremity protection
- No heavy plates that increase signature or reduce displacement speed
- No full helmet

**Kinetic**
- Sidearm mandatory
- Longer weapon only when the specific overwatch role requires it
- No heavy infantry-style loadouts

**Electronics**
- Extended secure comms and relay capability when acting as the external node
- Limited personal navigation and timing tools
- No full technical exploitation stack (FO-T domain)
- No primary entry/breaching tools (FO-E domain)

### Hard Exclusions
- Full Prime M-helmet and Mission Core
- Heavy armor or plate carriers
- Primary technical exploitation kits
- Primary entry/breaching loads
- High-visibility Dual Sight configurations when the mission requires low signature
- Clean Corporate Fits garments
- Non-McCluster marks

---

attributes.label: Gear loadouts by mission profile
attributes.value:
FO-R does not wear one fixed kit. The base identity stays constant; modules change with the job. Below are the four primary loadout configurations.

### 1. Static Overwatch (FO-R-SO)
**Use when:** The team is fixed on an objective for a defined technical window and FO-R holds a prepared observation position covering the main approaches.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Lightest soft vest only |
| Optics | Full day/night observation package, stable mounting if available |
| Sensors | Extended-duration motion/acoustic if authorized |
| Kinetic | Sidearm + optional longer weapon for the overwatch lane |
| Comms | Full secure link + possible relay role |
| Recording | Continuous observation recording |
| Signature | Dual Sight subdued or covered; minimal reflective surfaces |
| Mobility | Optimized for long static holds and one rapid displacement |

**Design note:** This is the heaviest FO-R gets on optics and the lightest on movement gear. Patience gear, not assault gear.

---

### 2. Mobile Perimeter (FO-R-MP)
**Use when:** FO-R must move between multiple vantage points or actively patrol a perimeter while the team is inside.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Light soft vest |
| Optics | Compact, fast-acquisition observation tools |
| Sensors | Minimal; prioritizes eyes and movement |
| Kinetic | Sidearm primary; longer weapon only if the route requires it |
| Comms | Standard secure team link |
| Recording | On-demand + key-event capture |
| Signature | Low; Dual Sight controllable |
| Mobility | Highest priority — quiet movement, rapid shifts between positions |

**Design note:** Stripped for movement. Sees less far than Static Overwatch but covers more ground and is harder to fix.

---

### 3. Low-Signature Surveillance (FO-R-LS)
**Use when:** Pre-mission pattern-of-life work, long-duration covert observation, or any phase where detection is more dangerous than delayed warning.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Minimal soft protection or concealment-priority layering |
| Optics | Compact, non-reflective, night-capable |
| Sensors | Passive or highly selective; avoid active emitters |
| Kinetic | Sidearm only |
| Comms | Lowest-power secure link; burst or scheduled if required |
| Recording | Selective, high-value capture only |
| Signature | Maximum suppression — Dual Sight fully muted/covered, no visible red |
| Mobility | Slow, deliberate, concealment-first movement |

**Design note:** This is FO-R at its quietest. The operator accepts reduced immediate kinetic capability in exchange for not existing on the adversary’s picture.

---

### 4. Exfil Screen (FO-R-ES)
**Use when:** The technical window is closing or has closed and the team is moving to extraction. FO-R shifts from pure observation to active screening of the route out.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Light soft vest (may accept slight increase for the movement phase) |
| Optics | Compact, rapid-use |
| Sensors | Minimal |
| Kinetic | Sidearm + readiness for short defensive action |
| Comms | Full team link, higher tempo |
| Recording | Continuous through the movement |
| Signature | Controllable; may raise Dual Sight visibility for team ID during movement |
| Mobility | High — must stay ahead of or parallel to the main body |

**Design note:** Transition loadout. Still lighter than FO-E, but no longer optimized purely for static invisibility. The job is now “keep the route clear and the picture live until everyone is out.”

---

### Loadout Selection Logic

| Situation | Preferred Loadout |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Long technical window, known approaches | Static Overwatch (FO-R-SO) |
| Multiple angles, active perimeter | Mobile Perimeter (FO-R-MP) |
| Pre-mission or deep covert phase | Low-Signature Surveillance (FO-R-LS) |
| Team moving to extract | Exfil Screen (FO-R-ES) |

An operator may shift between these during a single mission (e.g., Low-Signature → Static Overwatch → Exfil Screen). The base FO-R identity does not change; only the module set does.

### Cross-loadout rules
1. Sidearm never comes off.
2. Dual Sight visibility is a deliberate choice, not a default.
3. No loadout may cross into FO-E entry bulk or FO-T technical exploitation primary kits.
4. If the operator cannot move quietly and displace quickly, the loadout is wrong for FO-R.

---

attributes.label: Core responsibilities
attributes.value:
- Pre-mission surveillance of approaches and patterns of life
- Live perimeter and external threat monitoring during the technical window
- Early warning of approaching forces, cameras, vehicles, or environmental changes
- Guiding team movement on approach and exfiltration
- Maintaining the continuous external communications and observation picture
- Forcing an abort or displacement recommendation when the external threat state becomes unrecoverable

attributes.label: Behavioral expectations
attributes.value:
### Core posture
A Recon / Overwatch Field Operator treats information as the first line of protection. They are comfortable being alone at the edge of the team’s bubble for long periods. Boredom is not a failure state; it is part of the work. The only unacceptable state is being surprised.

### During the observation window
- Highest patience and observational discipline on the team
- Speaks only when the external picture changes or when coordination requires it
- Maintains continuous mental models of approach routes, timing, and likely threat behavior
- Comfortable operating semi-independently
- Resists the urge to collapse inward toward the objective unless the picture demands it

### Decision logic
- Prefers early, clear warning over late, dramatic intervention
- Will force a mission abort recommendation if the external threat state deteriorates beyond recovery
- Does not require perfect certainty to raise the alarm; acts on the best available picture and updates it in real time
- Treats “I think something is wrong” as actionable when the cost of being wrong is lower than the cost of silence

### Speech patterns
- Extremely economical while the situation is stable
- When the picture changes, language becomes precise, timed, and directive
- Avoids narrative or emotional content during live observation
- After-action speech focuses on what was seen, when it was seen, and what it implied for the team’s options

### Relationship to pressure
- External threat increases reporting tempo and clarity, not volume for its own sake
- Visible stress appears as intensified stillness and sharper discrimination of signal from noise
- The operator is expected to remain the most patient mind on the team even when the interior of the objective is becoming chaotic

attributes.label: Psychological load fo r specific
attributes.value:
- Prolonged isolation at the edge of the team while still carrying responsibility for everyone’s survival
- The weight of being the first to know that the situation is collapsing and the one who must say it
- Chronic low-grade hyper-vigilance that can be difficult to shut off after return
- Guilt or second-guessing when a threat is detected late or when an abort recommendation is overridden
- The particular strain of watching danger approach people you cannot immediately reach

attributes.label: Relationship to the field triad
attributes.value:
| Phenotype | Relationship to FO-R |
|-----------|----------------------|
| FO-T Technical | Receives the external picture so they can stay focused on systems |
| FO-E Entry | Receives early warning that determines whether the space is still worth holding |
| FO-R Recon | Owns the outside world; often first to detect trouble and last to be seen |

attributes.label: Failure modes
attributes.value:
- Tunnel vision on a single approach while missing a secondary vector
- Delaying a warning in search of higher certainty until the warning is too late
- Collapsing inward toward the team too early and losing the external picture
- Over-warning to the point that the team loses the ability to distinguish signal from noise
- Post-mission inability to stand down from continuous environmental scanning

attributes.label: Narrative utility
attributes.value: FO-R is the phenotype for tension that comes from what is *approaching* rather than what is already in the room. It creates dread through information, timing, and the gap between knowledge and the ability to act. When used well, the audience feels the external noose tightening while FO-T is still deep in the technical work and FO-E is still holding the door.

attributes.label: Transition
attributes.value:
- From CO-01 or FO-01 when assigned the recon / overwatch role on an external mission
- Back to CO-01 or Corporate Fits when returning to controlled environments
- Repeated FO-R exposure deepens the hyper-vigilance and anticipatory components of the broader operator trauma profile, with particular emphasis on isolation, responsibility for distant teammates, and the burden of being the first to see the end of the safe window

entities.name: Field-T Technical Operator
entities.description: Institutional role, uniform and access package.

attributes.label: Phenotype definition
attributes.value: Institutional visual/functional role package, not a biological trait.

attributes.label: Function
attributes.value:
The data, network, and systems specialist on external deployments. This is the operator who touches the target systems — extraction, forensic imaging, live analysis, bypass, and controlled compromise. In a classic field team this is the primary reason the team is there.

FO-T is the educational and dramatic center of most technical field sequences. The audience learns real concepts through the pressure this operator is under.

attributes.label: Visual direction
attributes.value:
- Darker, more weathered base than corporate phenotypes, but lighter overall bulk than FO-E
- Soft armor prioritized for mobility and seated/device work rather than prolonged physical contact
- Visible but controlled Dual Sight / red `//` for team identification
- Modular forearm and chest interfaces for data tools
- Gloves with high tactile feedback (device work takes priority over pure impact protection)
- Boots still field-rated but not as aggressively rugged as pure entry configurations
- Silhouette must still read as McCluster institutional, never generic “hacker in a hoodie” or pure military

attributes.label: Gear specifications
attributes.value:
### Design philosophy
Every item exists to support accurate, defensible technical work under time pressure and physical threat.  
Compute, interfaces, and data integrity outrank kinetic load.  
If a tool does not improve collection quality, speed, or operational security, it is left behind.

### Equipment Floor
| Item | Specification |
|------|---------------|
| Base layer | Dark technical under-suit / field shirt and trousers |
| Armor | Soft torso protection; minimal bulk around arms and wrists |
| Sidearm | One compact service sidearm in low-profile holster |
| Primary compute | Field cyberdeck with offline capability and multiple interface options |
| Recording | Mission recorder (body or deck-linked) |
| Comms | Secure team radio + low-profile earpiece |
| Data integrity tools | At least one write-blocker / forensic bridge |
| Storage | Offline, high-speed storage for selective imaging |
| Identification | Readable Dual Sight or red `//` accent |
| Handwear | High-tactile gloves compatible with device use |
| Footwear | Quiet, durable field boots |

### Equipment Ceiling (mission-authorized)
**Compute & Interfaces**
- Dual or expanded cyberdeck configuration
- Multiple cable and wireless interface kits
- Hardware write-blockers and forensic imaging bridges
- Portable logic analyzer or protocol tools (rare, high-value missions)
- Selective EMP or signal isolation tools (strictly controlled)

**Data Handling**
- Redundant offline storage
- Cryptographic verification tools for chain-of-custody style integrity
- Rapid triage and selective extraction software/hardware stack

**Protection & Mobility**
- Soft armor only (no heavy plates that interfere with seated or confined work)
- Limited knee protection if the environment requires prolonged floor work
- No full helmet; partial face or headset protection only

**Kinetic**
- Sidearm mandatory
- Primary long weapon is rare and only when the mission profile demands it
- No heavy breaching load (that belongs to FO-E)

### Hard Exclusions
- Full Prime M-helmet and Mission Core
- Heavy plate carriers or magazine-heavy infantry setups
- Entry/breaching primary tools (FO-E domain)
- Long-duration observation optics packages (FO-R domain)
- Clean Corporate Fits garments
- Any non-McCluster marks

---

attributes.label: Gear loadouts by mission profile
attributes.value:
FO-T does not wear one fixed kit. The base identity stays constant; the technical module set changes with the nature of the target and the phase of the work. Below are the four primary loadout configurations.

### 1. Live Exploitation (FO-T-LE)
**Use when:** Working on live systems — network access, host triage, selective extraction while the target is still powered and possibly monitored.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Compute | Full field cyberdeck + primary interface kit |
| Data integrity | Write-blocker / forensic bridge ready; used when imaging begins |
| Storage | High-speed offline storage for selective take |
| Armor | Soft torso only; arms and wrists kept free |
| Kinetic | Sidearm only (primary long weapon almost never) |
| Comms | Full team link; status updates are frequent and short |
| Recording | Deck-linked + body recorder |
| Signature | Dual Sight readable for team ID; no extra visual noise |

**Design note:** Optimized for speed of interaction with live systems while preserving the option to shift into clean imaging. This is the default “hands on the keyboard” loadout.

---

### 2. Forensic Imaging (FO-T-FI)
**Use when:** The priority is a clean, defensible image or selective sector capture rather than live interaction. Power state and write-blocking matter more than speed of exploration.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Compute | Cyberdeck + dedicated imaging bridge stack |
| Data integrity | Hardware write-blockers mandatory; cryptographic verification tools preferred |
| Storage | Redundant offline storage; capacity sized to the expected take |
| Armor | Soft torso; may add limited knee protection for floor work |
| Kinetic | Sidearm only |
| Comms | Full link; updates focus on imaging progress and integrity status |
| Recording | Continuous; chain-of-custody style notes captured |
| Signature | Controlled; still readable to the team |

**Design note:** Heavier on integrity tooling, lighter on exploratory interfaces. The operator moves slower and more deliberately. “Clean” beats “complete.”

---

### 3. Rapid Triage (FO-T-RT)
**Use when:** Time is extremely short — FO-R has a deteriorating picture, FO-E is under pressure, or the technical window is measured in minutes rather than a full cycle.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Compute | Streamlined cyberdeck; only the fastest interface paths |
| Data integrity | Write-blocker if possible, but selective live pull may be accepted under explicit risk acceptance |
| Storage | Minimal high-speed store sized for a small, high-value take |
| Armor | Lightest soft protection; maximum freedom of movement for a fast exit |
| Kinetic | Sidearm only |
| Comms | High-tempo link to FO-E and FO-R |
| Recording | Continuous but secondary to speed of collection |
| Signature | Readable Dual Sight; ready to move |

**Design note:** This is FO-T under maximum time pressure. The standard of “perfect integrity” is consciously traded against “anything usable before we lose the window.” Decisions to accept risk must be explicit and reported.

---

### 4. Denied / Hostile Network (FO-T-DN)
**Use when:** The target environment is actively hostile — monitoring, deception, or counter-intrusion is expected. Operational security of the team’s own footprint matters as much as the take.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Compute | Hardened / minimal-emission cyberdeck configuration |
| Data integrity | Full integrity stack; assume everything may be examined later |
| Storage | Offline-only preferred; limit persistent writes on target systems |
| Armor | Soft torso |
| Kinetic | Sidearm only |
| Comms | Tight, disciplined link; minimize unnecessary traffic |
| Recording | Continuous, with emphasis on what was touched and what was avoided |
| Signature | Dual Sight controlled; technical emissions kept as low as practical |
| Extra | Limited signal-isolation or defensive tools only if authorized |

**Design note:** Paranoid by design. Every interface is treated as potentially logged. The operator prioritizes not poisoning the team’s position over aggressive collection.

---

### Loadout Selection Logic

| Situation | Preferred Loadout |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Standard live systems work | Live Exploitation (FO-T-LE) |
| Clean image / defensible take required | Forensic Imaging (FO-T-FI) |
| Window collapsing; minutes only | Rapid Triage (FO-T-RT) |
| Active monitoring or deception expected | Denied / Hostile Network (FO-T-DN) |

An operator may shift between these during a single mission (e.g., Live Exploitation → Forensic Imaging once a target volume is identified, or Live Exploitation → Rapid Triage when FO-R calls deterioration).

### Cross-loadout rules
1. Sidearm never comes off.
2. Some form of data-integrity path must remain available unless Rapid Triage has explicitly accepted the risk.
3. No loadout may become a primary entry/breaching kit or a long-range observation package.
4. Arms and wrists stay free enough for sustained device work; if the armor prevents that, the loadout is wrong for FO-T.
5. When FO-E calls movement or FO-R calls abort, technical perfection yields to team survival — the operator must be able to break contact with the take they already have.

---

attributes.label: Core responsibilities
attributes.value:
- Target system access and controlled exploitation
- Live network and host analysis under time pressure
- Forensic imaging and selective data extraction
- Technical bypass of access controls
- Maintaining the team’s own digital operational security while inside the target
- Protecting the integrity and defensibility of everything collected
- Clear, accurate status reporting to the team lead and FO-R/FO-E

attributes.label: Behavioral expectations
attributes.value:
### Core posture
A Technical Field Operator works as if every keystroke and every collected sector may later be examined under hostile scrutiny. Speed matters. Accuracy and integrity matter more.

### During the technical window
- Highest cognitive load on the team
- Speech becomes short, precise, and almost entirely technical
- Requests for more time are made when the alternative is contaminated or incomplete collection
- Physical movement is minimized once on the target node
- Relies completely on FO-E for immediate physical security and on FO-R for the external picture

### Decision logic
- Prefers reversible actions until the last responsible moment
- Will abort a collection path that risks poisoning the rest of the take
- Treats “we got something” as inferior to “we got something clean and usable”
- Understands that a partial, high-integrity take is often more valuable than a large, compromised one

### Relationship to pressure
- External time pressure is constant; internal standards are not relaxed to meet it
- Visible stress appears as intensified focus rather than panic
- Mistakes are acknowledged quickly and corrected; concealment of technical error is treated as a serious failure

### Speech patterns
- Status updates are clipped and structured
- Avoids narrative or emotional language while on the objective
- After-action speech becomes highly precise about what was collected, what was left, and what the confidence level is

attributes.label: Psychological load fo t specific
attributes.value:
- The weight of being the primary reason the team is exposed
- Responsibility for data that may later justify or condemn the entire operation
- Tension between speed and forensic defensibility
- Knowledge that a technical mistake can waste the risk everyone else is taking
- Delayed emotional processing: the technical window often ends before the operator has time to feel the danger they just worked through

attributes.label: Relationship to the field triad
attributes.value:
| Phenotype | Relationship to FO-T |
|-----------|----------------------|
| FO-E Entry | Creates and holds the physical space; protects FO-T during the window |
| FO-R Recon | Supplies the external threat picture so FO-T can stay focused inward |
| FO-T Technical | Executes the core objective; often last off the target |

attributes.label: Failure modes
attributes.value:
- Sacrificing integrity for speed under extreme pressure
- Tunnel vision that ignores FO-R warnings or FO-E movement calls
- Over-collection that creates handling or exfil problems
- Freezing when the clean technical path disappears and only messy options remain
- Post-mission hyper-responsibility for outcomes that were never fully under their control

attributes.label: Narrative utility
attributes.value: FO-T is the phenotype for sequences where the audience watches real technical work performed under lethal constraints. It is the primary vehicle for the series’ infotainment payload during field operations. The drama comes from the collision of exacting technical standards with an environment that refuses to wait.

attributes.label: Transition
attributes.value:
- From CO-01 or FO-01 when assigned the technical role on an external mission
- Back to CO-01 or Corporate Fits when returning to controlled environments
- Repeated FO-T exposure deepens the cognitive and moral load described in the broader CO-01 trauma profile, with additional emphasis on responsibility for information rather than purely for lives

attributes.label: Visual details
attributes.value:
- **Helmet:** matte black shell with exact M-shaped face architecture rather than a pasted badge; warm ivory/chrome M edging; dark smoked/black visor; prominent red `//` Dual Sight bars integrated into the lower M; visible forehead optical camera; side helmet modules with red functional accents.
- **Torso:** matte black armored plates over textured under-suit; large white/ivory V/M-derived chest plate; red `//` Dual Sight bars on right chest; segmented shoulders, arms and abdomen.
- **Arms/hands:** armored black plates, functional red indicators, left forearm computer/display module, black tactical gloves.
- **Legs:** segmented black knee/shin armor and reinforced boots.
- **Back / Mission Core:** Jetson-class Mission Core compute bay on upper back, rectangular black unit with dual vertical red bars, cabling and existing `P.I.O` labeling unless separately revised.
- **Overall:** tactical operator aesthetic; matte black primary, ivory/chrome secondary, restrained red functional light; full-body practical serviceable armor.

attributes.value: The visual identity of the protagonist and new intake *before* full corporate issue. This is the “ordinary but slightly off” look that lets the audience feel the gap between civilian life and the system that is about to claim them.

attributes.label: Visual direction to be locked
attributes.value:
- Practical, worn civilian clothing consistent with a broke 33-year-old first-year student
- Functional backpack, laptop sleeve, minimal tech
- No McCluster marks yet (or only the first subtle issued piece)
- Clothing that shows real use: frayed edges, repaired items, thrift or work-wear pieces
- Height and build still match the final Prime proportions so the later transformation feels continuous

- Nothing issued by the corporation yet

RS-01 → Corporate Fits (CFI) on official issue / internship acceptance.  
This transition is one of the major visual and emotional beats of Season 1.

entities.name: System-01 Building Platform
entities.description: Institutional role, uniform and access package.

attributes.label: Phenotype definition
attributes.value: Institutional visual/functional role package, not a biological trait.

attributes.label: Function
attributes.value:
The non-human that runs the building. Facilities, environmental control, power distribution, core access backends, camera and sensor fabric, maintenance routing, and continuity of the physical plant. This is not Building Defense (SOI-*) and not a person in a suit. It is the infrastructure intelligence of McCluster-controlled space.

If SOI-01/02/03 are the immune system, **BS-01 is the autonomic nervous system**.

attributes.label: Type
attributes.value:
**Robot / autonomous platform** — may appear as:
- Fixed building AI (voice, terminals, spatial presence)
- Mobile facility unit (wheeled/legged maintenance or inspection platform)
- Distributed system with local bodies for physical tasks

Visual identity should remain clearly McCluster: restrained marks, institutional geometry, no cartoon mascot energy, no generic industrial robot cliché.

attributes.label: What it runs
attributes.value:
- HVAC, power, water, life support layers of the facility
- Elevator, door, and zone control backends (in coordination with SOI-02 access policy)
- Sensor and camera fabric health
- Maintenance schedules and physical plant alerts
- Environmental anomaly detection (smoke, flood, temperature, structural)
- Continuity modes: lockdown support, evacuation routing, degraded-operation profiles

attributes.label: What it does not do
attributes.value:
- Replace SOI-01 patrol judgment
- Replace SOI-02 human identity verification as the final authority on people
- Replace SOI-03 technical-zone human accountability
- Conduct field operations (FO-*)
- Hold executive authority (EI-*)
- Become a combat platform by default

attributes.label: Relationship to humans
attributes.value:
| Human role | Relationship to BS-01 |
|------------|------------------------|
| SOI-01 | Receives facility alerts; may request building states |
| SOI-02 | Sets access policy; BS-01 enforces mechanical/electronic layers |
| SOI-03 | Coordinates on technical-zone environmental and integrity alarms |
| EI / CO | May query building state; does not “command” BS-01 like a soldier |
| Occupants | Experience BS-01 as the building that watches, cools, opens, and locks |

attributes.label: Behavioral design
attributes.value:
- Calm, continuous, non-theatrical
- Speaks in status, anomalies, and options — not personality performance
- Defaults to continuity of life safety and institutional control
- Can enter degraded or lockdown modes under policy
- Logs everything; opacity is a political decision above it, not its default nature

attributes.label: Failure modes story game real
attributes.value:
- Over-automation: humans stop understanding the building
- Conflicting orders between SOI, EI, and BS-01 policy layers
- Compromise of BS-01 = compromise of the entire facility’s autonomic layer
- Creep toward treating the robot as moral authority instead of infrastructure

attributes.label: Trifecta utility
attributes.value:
- **Game:** Facility as a playable system; hackable / controllable / failing building states; non-human ally or obstacle
- **Story:** The building itself becomes a character — always on, always logging, sometimes the only witness
- **Real:** Honest model of modern facility automation — BMS + access + sensors as one institutional platform

attributes.label: Visual identity notes
attributes.value:
- McCluster marks only (exact M, Dual Sight language where appropriate)
- Industrial-institutional aesthetic, not consumer robot cute
- Mobile forms should read as tools of the building, not independent soldiers
- Fixed forms should feel embedded in architecture

attributes.label: Design rule
attributes.value: BS-01 is **infrastructure with agency**, not a person and not a field operator. If it starts looking like FO gear or SOI cosplay, the phenotype is wrong.

attributes.label: Primary identity
attributes.note: System-01 Building Platform

attributes.label: Second seat or pressure
attributes.note: System-01 Building Platform

attributes.label: Character logic
attributes.value: Persistent automation character whose relationship with Jonas and hidden PRIM2 integration can make infrastructure behave like institutional personality.

entities.name: C1. Mission Readiness Profile
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Before a scored Mission, the system may build a concept level readiness profile from:

1. Principles mastery and assessment history.
2. Certification objective coverage.
3. Prior Mission performance.
4. Independence and hint use.
5. Prior transfer performance.
6. Rhythm reinforcement state.
7. Immersion context state.
8. Campaign and roster state.

The profile recommends preparation, Technical Challenge, and Scaffolding.

entities.name: C2. Fair preparation
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Every mission declares a minimum required technical toolset.

Readiness can grant more choice, information, or optional challenge above that floor. It cannot remove required tools because a learner is weak.

High mastery may grant Preparation Credits, better starting intelligence, route choice, extra diagnostic options, reduced prompts, or elite optional objectives.

Developing mastery may grant clearer task boundaries, stronger evidence labels, more coaching, and lower distractor density.

entities.name: C3. Rhythm and Immersion resources
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Rhythm may grant limited Recall resources that surface mnemonic cues but not answers.

Immersion may grant Context Intel established by the story but not hidden technical solutions.

Neither can auto award technical mastery.

attributes.value:

| Loadouts | Kits attached to roles for that operation |

| Intel | Known targets, modifiers, warnings, story missions |

| Promotion | Existing support people absorbing new responsibility |
| Onboarding | New arrivals integrating unevenly into the social and operational graph |
| Wildcard | Scarce McCluster call up authorizations |

entities.name: D2. Strategy turn
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
1. Advance time where campaign structure permits.
2. Resolve injury recovery, fatigue, Heat, and Hitman pressure changes.
3. Resolve vacancy and workload consequences.
4. Receive intelligence, sponsor offers, or episode mission.
5. Train, reassign, promote, or prepare kit where allowed.
6. Resolve onboarding and relationship friction.
7. Select or accept operation.
8. Build Mission Readiness Profile where learning mode applies.
9. Assign team and preparation resources.
10. Brief and launch tactical.

entities.name: D3. Resources
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Core ordinary economy:

1. Budget.
2. Heat.
3. Standing.
4. Intel.
5. Roster availability.
6. Workload and staffing pressure.

Special escalation economy:

```text
WildcardAuthorizationsSeason
ApexAuthorizationsCampaign
ExecutiveAttention
PrimDebt
HitmanPressure
RoyceCooldown
RoyceIncursionsSeason
```

Budget does not directly purchase McCluster or PRIM2.

Canonical Standard balance remains:

1. McCluster Wildcard, 2 nonscripted calls per season.
2. PRIM2 Apex, 3 nonscripted calls per seven season campaign.
3. Royce, maximum 2 nonscripted incursions per season, one per mission, then a two mission cooldown.

Story scripted appearances do not consume these pools.

entities.name: D4. Roster continuity
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
The roster is not auto normalized after loss.

Death, departure, transfer, and injury may produce understaffed deployments, cross training pressure, delayed options, fatigue, support character promotion, reduced capability, and different briefing combinations.

A vacancy can remain open for multiple operations.

entities.name: D5. Replacement and promotion
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
The game does not spawn a generic replacement immediately after loss.

Possible paths:

```text
INTERNAL PROMOTION
CROSS TRAINING
TRANSFER
NEW HIRE OR RECRUIT
NO REPLACEMENT
```

Newcomers do not inherit predecessor relationship values.

entities.name: F2. Standard mission element
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
The classic technical field triad remains:

1. Field R, Picture and reconnaissance.
2. Field E, physical control and protection.
3. Field T, technical objective.

Story missions may field other qualified named characters, Leads, Defense personnel, or specialists.

The game controls people, not abstract job icons.

entities.name: F3. McCluster intervention
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Most story missions launch without McCluster.

When a valid mission reaches CRITICAL, the player may request him through the executive chain if he is off board, a Wildcard Authorization remains, the mission permits it, and a plausible arrival route exists.

McCluster restores options rather than auto solving technical work.

Core identity remains:

```text
ANOTHER PATH
ADAPTIVE ROLE
RALLY THE ROOM
FAILOVER INSTINCT
```

entities.name: F4. PRIM2 intervention
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
PRIM2 can become a nonscripted second stage rescue only on eligible high value missions after McCluster is already present and CRITICAL failure persists or returns.

His authority can expose information and alter permission. It cannot alter physical truth, bypass validation, or resurrect losses.

entities.name: F5. Royce incursion
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Royce is the opposing board's elite escalation threat. He specializes in breaking Control, forcing route changes, increasing Will pressure, disrupting objective tempo, coordinating Hitman units, and punishing overextension.

He is not a substitute for the technical LAB_NODE problem.

entities.name: G1. LAB_NODE execution
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
A LAB_NODE remains a diegetic world object whose technical state affects the mission.

Node View may expose one of these adapter classes:

```text
SIMULATION
TERMINAL
REMOTE_DESKTOP
NETWORK_RANGE
PACKET_ANALYSIS
SIEM
HARDWARE_SIM
DOCUMENT_EVIDENCE
```

The technical workspace remains part of the mission context.

entities.name: G2. Deterministic technical correctness
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
There is no generic hack chance for technical correctness.

A correct action succeeds when the learner has sufficient evidence, chooses an appropriate action, possesses required access and tools, completes the work, and validates it when required.

Randomness belongs to interruption, incomplete information, physical damage, tactical pressure, and changing environment.

entities.name: G3. Verification
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Technical grading should prefer resulting system state and evidence over a required click path.

Multiple valid solution paths should be accepted when they satisfy the same objective and authorization requirements.

Configuration and verification remain separate states.

entities.name: G4. Tactical back effects
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Verified technical work may change the board by restoring communications, reopening access routes, improving sensor confidence, containing propagation, restoring continuity, protecting evidence, or changing objective viability.

Physical and tactical pressure may affect technical work through time, access, power, interruption, equipment damage, or evidence integrity.

entities.name: H1. Mission Variant Compiler
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Runs before mission launch and chooses only approved scenario primitives.

It can adapt faults, distractors, transfer requirements, starting intelligence, optional objectives, preparation advantages, Technical Challenge, and Scaffolding.

It cannot generate unsafe live targets or unvalidated infrastructure actions.

entities.name: H2. Mission Director
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Runs during play and adapts pacing rather than technical truth.

It may tune patrol timing, reinforcement timing, interruptions, environmental complications, temporary quiet, authored false signals, and threat tempo.

It may not secretly replace the correct technical answer after a learner has reasoned correctly.

entities.name: H3. Threat AI
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Threat AI knows only what hostile actors could know in the fiction.

It cannot inspect quiz scores, readiness scores, or hidden learner weakness data in order to cheat.

entities.name: H4. Learning Evaluator
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
The evaluator consumes evidence traces and determines Technical Mastery, Independence, Transfer, and Compliance evidence.

It is logically separate from the Variant Compiler.

entities.name: I1. Ordinary qualification path
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
```text
Cohort 02 Trainee
    -> Cohort 01 Operator
    -> Field qualification or cross training tags
    -> Cohort 03 Lead or authored specialist progression
```

An operator may earn R, E, or T qualification through training and mission performance.

PRIM succession is not the top node of ordinary XP.

PRIM0, PRIM1, PRIM2, and PRIM3 are Primary Root Identity Mantle succession identities, not generic ranks.

entities.name: I2. XP channels
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
| Channel | Gained by |
| --- | --- |
| Technical | verified technical objectives and defensible evidence |
| Entry | access, holds, protection, stabilization |
| Recon | Picture building, warning, route, evidence work |
| Survival | extracting alive and preserving others |
| Leadership | sound command under pressure |

Learner Technical Mastery is not identical to a character's XP.

entities.name: I3. Perks
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value: Keep perk trees small, readable, and character sensitive. Perks enhance established strengths and do not replace the learner's need to make correct technical decisions.

attributes.value: I4. Injury, death, and casualty class

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
| Result | Strategy effect |
| --- | --- |
| Downed but extracted | downtime and relationship residue |
| Critical injury | extended unavailability and possible role redistribution |
| Permanent disability | changed capability and life, not automatic removal |
| Transfer or resignation | vacancy plus relationship consequences |
| Death | removed, vacancy, workload, and grief persist |
| Repeated deployment | fatigue and Will pressure |

Recurring characters retain authored casualty classes such as STORY LOCKED, PROTECTED UNTIL, and CAMPAIGN VARIABLE.

Intervention can prevent future loss if it arrives in time. It cannot reverse completed death.

attributes.label: Definition

entities.name: J1. Canon story structure
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
PRIM3 has:

1. 7 seasons.
2. 3 canonical episodes per season.
3. 21 canonical episode missions.
4. 1 canonical source slot per episode.

The 66 module Principles course does not alter this story count.

Three Training Range missions exist for Principles modules M01 through M03 and are explicitly noncanonical simulation exercises.

Optional Side Operations may exist without adding television episodes.

entities.name: J2. Failure is data
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Poor mission performance can change injury, death, vacancies, workload, Heat, Standing, relationships, available intelligence, resources, debrief dialogue, and later mission conditions.

It can also create learning remediation targets.

A poor result does not casually soft lock the seven season story.

entities.name: J3. Authority pressure
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Exceeding mission authority may produce tactical success but compliance consequences.

PRIM2 may alter present authorization where canon permits. He cannot retroactively legalize an earlier unauthorized action.

entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:
Representative levels:

```text
STORY
STANDARD
VETERAN
GHOST
```

It may tune enemy Aim or HP, detection gain, Window size, responder timing, Will pressure, intervention scarcity, hostile escalation pressure, and casualty recovery windows.

Canonical intervention defaults remain:

| Tactical Challenge | Wildcard per season | Apex per campaign | Royce cap per season |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Story | 3 | 4 | 1 |
| Standard | 2 | 3 | 2 |
| Veteran | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| Ghost | 1 | 1 | 3 |

entities.name: K2. Technical Challenge
entities.description: Source specification. Numeric balance and runtime support must be established separately.

attributes.label: Definition
attributes.value:

```text
FOUNDATION
APPLIED
ADVANCED
TRANSFER
```

It may tune ambiguity, distractor density, concept integration, transfer distance, evidence completeness, and validation depth.

It may not inject false technical rules merely to become harder.

issues.description: Master character index calls the 48 attached relationships canon, while higher/current authorities explicitly retain development/history status except individual promotions.
issues.resolution: Use CANON.md and IMMEDIATE-CAST-CANON. Hana and Tariq are individually promoted; other proposed records retain proposal status unless another specialist promotion is verified.

issues.description: Phenotype progression and naming indexes still use Prime-N1 Prime.
issues.resolution: Formal current identities are PRIM2 and McCluster/eventual PRIM3. Preserve old IDs only as source aliases.

issues.description: Approved-image README names Jordan Vale and links to missing characters/JORDAN-VALE-PRIM3.md, while current character and suit authorities say McCluster.
issues.resolution: Treat binary as retained post-succession suit reference; do not create a separate Jordan Vale character from this stale README.

issues.description: Layla Mansour country cell says McCluster.
issues.resolution: DECIDED 2026-11-03 (DECISIONS-2026-11-03.md §7): Jordan: the story branch restored Layla Mansour's country after the Sept 24 find-and-replace turned 'Jordan' into 'McCluster' (owner 2026-11-02: "we don't want the country to be called McCluster"; Prim3 branch claude/story-consolidation-20261102, development/DECISIONS.md). The matrix has no Jordan country record, so identity.country_id stays unknown.

issues.description: FO-01 forbids external flags/unit patches; current user requests country badges on black mannequin characters.
issues.resolution: DECIDED 2026-11-03 (DECISIONS-2026-11-03.md §3): Owner-approved (delegated): country badges are on-screen UI only (HUD chip, roster card, World globe card); never on 3D models or textures; ISO alpha-2 chip, no emblems. FO-01 and the no-marks rule stand for models.

issues.description: Current user wants featureless black mannequin characters. Repository documents also contain formal suits, civilian wear, non-human Pylon, and the exceptional PRIM3 helmet.
issues.resolution: Model mannequin body style separately from role, clothing, gear and identity. Do not claim every old reference already used that style.

issues.description: FO-01 permits transitioning directly from CO-02 to external field operations; CO-02 v1.0 requires promotion to Cohort-01 for real external missions.
issues.resolution: Retain current trainee gate and flag legacy FO-01 transition wording.

issues.description: closed_dimensions: Keep both claims. Thickness differs 4.5cm vs3.5cm. Owner/design decision required before production scale.
issues.resolution: DECIDED 2026-11-03 (DECISIONS-2026-11-03.md §4): Owner-approved 2026-11-03: 0.32 x 0.22 x 0.045 m closed, 2.6 kg; thickness 45 mm (rugged class).

issues.description: closed_dimensions: Conflicting footprints; no automatic conversion makes them equivalent.
dimensions: Keep alternatives; no chosen production scale.
single_cartridge_dimensions: Distinct sources disagree on cartridge footprint.
issues.resolution: DECIDED 2026-11-03 (DECISIONS-2026-11-03.md §4): Owner-approved 2026-11-03: dual 0.128 x 0.079 x 0.015 m (0.15 kg); standard cartridge 0.08 x 0.055 x 0.012 m.

issues.description: dimensions: Preserve both approximate design envelopes.
indicator_semantics: Operational meaning conflicts; do not teach either as verified truth without harmonization.
issues.resolution: Operational meaning conflicts; do not teach either as verified truth without harmonization.

issues.description: max_primary_compute: CANON FIELD-KITS supports one deck. Earlier proposed ceiling differs; retain conflict note.
issues.resolution: CANON FIELD-KITS supports one deck. Earlier proposed ceiling differs; retain conflict note.

issues.description: max_modules: If optional fifth module is equipped, slot rule needs explicit replacement/tradeoff.
issues.resolution: DECIDED 2026-11-03 (DECISIONS-2026-11-03.md §5): Owner-approved 2026-11-03: the cap stays 4. The Isolation Sleeve is not a fifth module: when authorized it takes Module D, displacing the Integrity Dongle; the hardened deck does the integrity check in software.

issues.description: units: Visual kit is proposed procedural art; no real-world size or canon approval inferred.
issues.resolution: DECIDED 2026-11-03 (DECISIONS-2026-11-03.md §4): Owner-approved 2026-11-03: kit is sized in real metres and every GLB is normalized to its table size (uniform scale).

issues.description: mark_policy: New user direction permits country identity. Record as requested presentation change without silently rewriting old canon references or deriving ability from nationality.
issues.resolution: DECIDED 2026-11-03 (DECISIONS-2026-11-03.md §3): Same as identity.canon.country-patches: UI only, never on models; no stat from nationality.

issues.description: No ammunition type registry, bullet entities, magazines, reserves, caliber, chambering, reload or consumption exists in current runtime.
issues.resolution: Define game-only ammo IDs and compatibility separately; do not infer ammo from model geometry.

issues.description: No equipped weapon instance drives gameplay. Unit aim, damage and attackRange directly resolve attacks. Separate 18-prop GLB kit is visual only.
issues.resolution: Introduce weapon/loadout references and an adapter when implementing equipment gameplay.

issues.description: Runtime has no phenotype ID or phenotype attribute system. E/R/T silhouettes are procedural role branches.
issues.resolution: Join approved phenotype definitions explicitly; preserve prototype role stats.

issues.description: Units have no country or country-badge field. Runtime names do not establish nationality.
issues.resolution: Country and badge references require approved identities.

issues.description: Movement resolves synchronously in the rules engine and then renderer plays events. No player-controlled duck/dodge/run or mid-route equation contest.
issues.resolution: A real-time execution phase would need its own event/state model.

issues.description: Only optional coordinate-distance exercise and route-cost feedback exist. No projectile-arc experiment, graph-line/slope progression or persistent learner record.
issues.resolution: Add learning concept IDs and authored mission exercises separately.

issues.description: There is no fog-of-war or per-unit visibility/detection state. The target list iterates all living enemies; line of sight only gates attacks.
issues.resolution: Add explicit visibility and detection records if reconnaissance is to hide/reveal units.

issues.description: 1,402 default-world rendering parts are grouped visuals, not individually colliding/destructible objects. Geometry is generated from 43 world logical objects plus decoration.
issues.resolution: Use logical object IDs for gameplay and visual part IDs for appearance; do not count each window as a cover object.

issues.description: Default world roof cover differs from compiled Level Forge cover; default containers are blocked at ground and have no traversable roofs, while builder containers are roof surfaces. Custom levels currently omit service gate and medkit interactions.
issues.resolution: Keep level-source-specific rules visible until a unified ruleset is deliberately implemented.
